| Device without an identity                | Use initial enrollment. For an existing entry, check the replacement restriction in [provisioning](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/provisioning-strategies).                  |
| Retired device                            | Review the operational decision before readmission. Decommissioned state and revocation of the entire history are not equivalent.                                                  |
| Timeout, HTTP 500 or installation failure | Inspect the device, issued certificates and history before retrying. A successor may have been issued or the previous identity revoked.                                            |

Continuous operation [#continuous-operation]

Schedule renewal with time for disconnections, trust distribution and consumer checks. Stagger requests across the population and bound retries within the window; authentication, subject and policy errors require correcting their cause. Maintain an admitted and tested recovery mechanism for lost keys and pairs that could not be installed.

Continue with [Trust distribution](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/trust-distribution), [Devices and identities](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/device-management) and [Troubleshooting](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/troubleshooting).


# Enrollment troubleshooting (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/troubleshooting)



Diagnose one operation and device at a time. Record the DMS/APS, endpoint, time, HTTP code, presented serial and CSR CN. Retain the response without including private keys or webhook credentials in the report.

Diagnostics and compatibility [#diagnostics-and-compatibility]

Error codes and diagnostics [#error-codes-and-diagnostics]

The EST controller normally returns 400 when rejecting input and 500 when the service rejects or fails the operation. A 500 can also represent a policy denial; it does not mean retrying is safe. Gateway can produce its own codes and bodies. Examine the actual body and persisted result.

| Symptom or message                                          | What to check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| curl rejects TLS, name or issuer                            | URL, clock, server SAN and approved root in `est-trust.pem`. Resolve trust in [Deployment](/docs/deployment/troubleshooting); do not skip verification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 404 or missing APS                                          | Public route `/.well-known/est/{DMS_ID}/{operation}` and existing DMS. APS is not the service name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 400, CSR or format error                                    | `Content-Type: application/pkcs10`, Base64 of DER, valid signature and a body preserved without double encoding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Missing credential or invalid certificate                   | Operation mode, validating CA, dates, revocation and credential delivery by Gateway. Do not confuse server TLS trust with the bootstrap CA.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Webhook denies, times out or responds without authorization | Configuration, connectivity and JSON response with `authorized: true`. There is no automatic fallback to `NO_AUTH`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `unexpected status code: <n>: redirects are not followed`   | The webhook answered with a redirect. Configure the final absolute `http` or `https` URL in the webhook config; redirects are never followed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `webhook response exceeds 1048576 bytes`                    | The receiver returned more than 1 MiB of JSON. Reduce the response of the authorization webhook.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `webhook config must not reference files`                   | The webhook config points to files (`ca_cert_file`, `mtls_options.cert_file`, `mtls_options.key_file`). For mTLS, enter the certificate and key as Base64-encoded PEM in `cert_content` and `key_content`, or as plain PEM; remove any other file field, including `ca_cert_file`, which has no inline equivalent (the receiver certificate must chain to the system trust store). See the webhook credentials guidance in [DMS](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/dms#external-webhook-settings). |
| `mtls_options.cert_content must be base64-encoded PEM`      | The value is neither Base64-encoded PEM nor plain PEM: it is a file path or Base64 of non-PEM data. Enter the certificate and key as Base64-encoded PEM, like certificates elsewhere in the API, or as plain PEM (see the webhook settings in [DMS](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/dms#external-webhook-settings)). The same message names `mtls_options.key_content` when the key is the offending value.                                                                                      |
| `webhook mTLS certificate and key are invalid: …`           | The certificate and key do not form a matching pair. Enter both values from the same pair; the check runs when the DMS is saved and again on every webhook call.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 400 `struct validation error` creating or updating a DMS    | The webhook config of the operation that uses it is invalid. Review `external_webhook_settings` in [DMS](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/dms#external-webhook-settings).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| HTTP 500 with an `err` body on enroll or reenroll           | Service failures reach the EST client as 500 with a body of `err` plus the message; webhook authorization errors are named there.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `device not preregistered`                                  | PRE\_REGISTRATION requires an existing inventory entry.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `forbiddenNewEnrollment`                                    | An existing device requires replacement to be enabled, even in No Identity. Investigate before enabling the flag.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Different owning DMS                                        | CN/ID, global inventory and owning DMS; do not reuse an ID from another context.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `invalid RawSubject bytes`                                  | CSR subject versus the current certificate. Preserve its attributes as well as its CN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `invalid reenroll window`                                   | Current identity's NotAfter and reenrollment\_delta. Alert thresholds do not change that window.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Current certificate revoked                                 | Renewal rejected; prepare authorized recovery according to the cause.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| CA, profile or signing error                                | Active CA, available key, selected profile and restrictions. Successful cacerts does not prove issuance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| HTTP 200 without a device connection                        | Installed pair, chain, uses, consumer trust and permissions. Also check the slot and history.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Timeout or error after issuance                             | New certificates, current slot and previous identity's state before retrying.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Compatibility notes [#compatibility-notes]

The examples use the contract of the [examined backend](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/overview#contract-version). Do not automatically attribute that behavior to another release. Check the saved renewal mode and Gateway behavior with expired certificates and the bootstrap CA.

The default response is Base64-encoded DER PKCS#7; PEM through `Accept: application/x-pem-file` is a Lamassu extension. ServerKeyGen returns multipart and requires handling each part separately. See the [EST reference](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/est-reference).

EST enrollment fails [#est-enrollment-fails]

1. Check HTTPS with the approved root and query cacerts for the correct APS.
2. Review the saved DMS: protocol, registration, authentication for that operation, CA, profile and window.
3. Verify the CSR locally and relate its CN to the inventory.
4. Make one request, save headers/body and query the device and certificates.
5. If you receive an identity, check the key, subject, use and connection with the consumer.

External bootstrap revocation checks have limitations: absence of evidence can be accepted, and OCSP Unknown does not cause the same rejection as Revoked. Do not assume a policy that rejects every uncertainty. An intermediate CA in the TLS chain does not prove that the entire chain reached the DMS validator either.

For logs, networking, pods or Gateway headers, continue in [Deployment troubleshooting](/docs/deployment/troubleshooting). For identities issued, revoked or bound partially, use [Renewal and recovery](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/renewal-and-recovery) and [Devices and identities](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/device-management).


# Trust distribution and updates (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/trust-distribution)



This guide is for device and consumer trust administrators. You need issuer inventory, trust-store access and an authenticated update channel. Distributing certificates is separate from choosing trusted anchors.

Three trust relationships [#three-trust-relationships]

| Relationship        | Material prepared by its owner                                         |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Device → EST server | Previously verified server root, chain or pin and TLS name.            |
| DMS → requester     | CAs and rules authorizing initial or renewal credentials.              |
| Consumer → device   | Operational identity roots, intermediates, validation and permissions. |

Obtaining a certificate does not automatically configure these relationships in third parties. Review the [Trust model](/docs/platform/pki/concepts/trust-model).

What cacerts returns [#what-cacerts-returns]

The DMS may include the available downstream TLS certificate, selected Managed CAs and enrollment CA. Selecting the issuer does not include every ancestor. The set may contain leaves, roots and intermediates, including multiple hierarchies during migration.

Position does not define the chain. Identify certificates by subject, issuer, AKI/SKI, signature and constraints. Download and inspect using [EST client](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/est-client#download-and-inspect-cacerts).

Install the required material [#install-the-required-material]

1. Keep initial EST server trust separate from identity consumer trust.
2. Select policy-approved roots as anchors.
3. Retain intermediates for chain building or presentation; do not automatically turn them into roots.
4. Present the leaf and required intermediates in mTLS. Normally the peer already trusts its root and does not need it sent.
5. Verify chain, dates, names, usages and revocation from the consumer.

Do not indiscriminately use all of `cacerts.pem` as `-CAfile`: this can expand trusted authorities, hide missing intermediates or trust a TLS leaf intended for another purpose.

Migrate trust [#migrate-trust]

Before changing Enrollment CA, inventory disconnected equipment, bootstrap and operational certificates, and consumers. Distribute the new root and required intermediates; check that a cohort accepts both old and new chains.

In the DMS, separate distributed CAs from the re-enrollment validation CAs at `reenrollment_settings.est_rfc7030_settings.client_certificate_settings.validation_cas`, used for re-enrollment credentials. That list is optional because the enrollment CA always validates re-enrollment credentials, but when switching the enrollment CA, add the previous issuance CA to it so old-CA identities keep re-enrolling during overlap. The inspected validator tries the enrollment CA followed by those CAs against the received leaf; accepting a multilevel chain requires checking what reaches the service and which issuer is configured.

Switch issuance, renew in cohorts and compare the installed serial with the active slot. Remove previous trust once no legitimate equipment needs it and policy permits ending overlap. Follow [Hierarchy and rotation](/docs/platform/pki/ca-hierarchy-and-rotation) for the PKI operation.

Check the update [#check-the-update]

Test an old identity allowed during overlap, a new one, an unknown chain and the result after removing old trust. Keep trust-store version, approved set, date and result. Reachable `/cacerts` establishes distribution only; it does not establish installation or acceptance across every device.


# AWS IoT Core (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/iot-fleets/integrations/aws-iot-core)



Lamassu's integration with AWS IoT Core bridges the PKI managed by Lamassu and AWS's connectivity platform. When a device obtains its certificate through the EST enrollment process, the connector ensures that certificate and its associated identity are recognized in AWS IoT Core without manual intervention. The result is that the device can authenticate directly to AWS with the same X.509 certificate Lamassu issued.

From a protocol standpoint, the device authenticates to AWS IoT Core via mutual TLS (mTLS): it presents its Lamassu-issued X.509 certificate as the client certificate, and AWS IoT Core verifies the certificate chain up to the CA registered in the account. Lamassu acts as the certification authority (CA); the connector ensures that CA is registered in AWS and that the device's certificate is known to the platform before the device attempts to connect (in `auto` mode) or on its first connection (in JITP mode).

This document is aimed both at the PKI administrator, who needs to configure the connector and register CAs, and at the device firmware developer, who needs to understand how Things are named, how the Device Shadow works and what happens when a certificate is revoked. For the firmware developer, the most important fact is that **the AWS Thing name (ThingName) always corresponds to the Common Name (CN) of the certificate issued by Lamassu**, regardless of the provisioning mode.

Connector architecture [#connector-architecture]

The AWS IoT Core connector is an independent Go process, a binary or container separate from Lamassu's core. In a monolithic deployment it is compiled by default (build tag `!noaws`) and activated with `aws_iot_manager.enabled: true` in the configuration file. In distributed deployments, it runs as its own container with access to Lamassu's CA, DMS Manager and Device Manager services over HTTP.

The connector does not poll Lamassu's services periodically. Instead, it **subscribes to Lamassu's internal event bus** (AMQP or AWS SQS/SNS, configurable) and reacts to the events it cares about: CA creation or update, DMS creation or update, device identity binding, certificate status change, certificate metadata update and device metadata update. This event-driven model ensures synchronization with AWS is nearly immediate and produces no polling load.

To avoid infinite loops, the connector ignores any event whose CloudEvent `source` field matches its own origin URI. This prevents the metadata writes the connector itself performs from re-triggering the same flow.

When several connectors run in parallel, for example for different AWS accounts, each instance has its own `connector_id`. All metadata the connector writes to Lamassu is stored under the key `lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}`, allowing coexistence without collisions.

Prerequisites [#prerequisites]

Before enabling the connector you need an AWS account with the proper IAM permissions and the connector correctly configured. The deployment process (Docker Compose, Kubernetes or binary) is described in the [deployment documentation](/docs/deployment/overview).

Required IAM permissions [#required-iam-permissions]

The IAM identity operating the connector needs at minimum the following permissions on the target account's resources:

| IAM action                                             | Purpose                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `iot:GetRegistrationCode`                              | Obtain the verification code for CA registration in the Primary Account |
| `iot:RegisterCACertificate`                            | Register the CA in AWS IoT                                              |
| `iot:DescribeCACertificate`                            | Check the CA registration status                                        |
| `iot:CreateThing` / `iot:UpdateThing`                  | Create or update Things in IoT Core                                     |
| `iot:RegisterThing`                                    | Provision Things through a template                                     |
| `iot:RegisterCertificate`                              | Register device certificates                                            |
| `iot:UpdateCertificate`                                | Change a certificate's status (ACTIVE / INACTIVE / REVOKED)             |
| `iot:CreatePolicy` / `iot:AttachPolicy`                | Create and attach IoT policies                                          |
| `iot:CreateThingGroup` / `iot:AddThingToThingGroup`    | Manage Thing groups                                                     |
| `iot:CreateProvisioningTemplate`                       | Create JITP templates                                                   |
| `iotdata:GetThingShadow` / `iotdata:UpdateThingShadow` | Read and write the Device Shadow                                        |

The forced-disconnect mechanism after revocation also requires access to the AWS IoT data plane API (`iot:Connect` with SigV4 over WebSocket), negotiated implicitly with the connector's credentials.

Configuration parameters [#configuration-parameters]

| Parameter                      | Type   | Required                       | Description                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connector_id`                 | string | Yes                            | Unique identifier of this connector instance. Used as the metadata namespace: `lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}`. |
| `aws_config.region`            | string | Yes                            | AWS region where the connector operates.                                                                       |
| `aws_config.auth_method`       | string | Yes                            | Authentication method: `static`, `role` or empty (SDK default credential chain).                               |
| `aws_config.access_key_id`     | string | Only with `auth_method=static` | AWS access key.                                                                                                |
| `aws_config.secret_access_key` | string | Only with `auth_method=static` | AWS secret key.                                                                                                |
| `aws_config.session_token`     | string | No                             | Session token (with `auth_method=static`).                                                                     |
| `aws_config.role_arn`          | string | Only with `auth_method=role`   | ARN of the role to assume.                                                                                     |
| `aws_config.endpoint_url`      | string | No                             | Alternative URL for all AWS services (useful with LocalStack in tests).                                        |
| `subscriber_event_bus`         | object | Yes                            | Configuration of the event bus the connector subscribes to (AMQP or AWS SQS/SNS).                              |
| `dms_manager_client`           | string | Yes                            | HTTP URL of Lamassu's DMS Manager service.                                                                     |
| `device_manager_client`        | string | Yes                            | HTTP URL of Lamassu's Device Manager.                                                                          |
| `ca_client`                    | string | Yes                            | HTTP URL of Lamassu's CA service.                                                                              |

Resource state machine [#resource-state-machine]

The connector owns the AWS side of four resource types — CAs, DMS provisioning templates (JITP), device certificates and Things. This section maps the bus events the connector consumes to the AWS resources they touch and to the AWS calls each transition performs. AWS resources are referenced with the notation `IoTCore/<resource>`.

Events the connector handles [#events-the-connector-handles]

The **CloudEvent type** column lists the event name on Lamassu's internal event bus; the **IAM actions** column lists the exact AWS SDK operations each flow invokes, so the required permissions can be derived directly from this table.

<div data-full-bleed-table>
  | CloudEvent type                                                      | Lamassu resource     | AWS Resource                                            | IAM actions                                                                                                                                                                              | AWS calls and effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Where in this page                                            |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `EventCreateCAKey` / `EventImportCAKey` / `EventUpdateCAMetadataKey` | CA                   | `IoTCore/CACertificate`                                 | `iot:GetRegistrationCode`, `iot:RegisterCACertificate`, `iot:DescribeCACertificate`, `iot:ListCACertificates`                                                                            | Loads the CA into connector state; a `registration.status = REQUESTED` write fires the registration flow (Primary with verification certificate, or SNI-only) and writes `SUCCEEDED` or `FAILED` back to the CA's metadata.                                          | [CA registration states](#ca-registration-states)             |
  | `EventCreateDMSKey` / `EventUpdateDMSKey`                            | DMS                  | `IoTCore/ProvisioningTemplate`                          | `iot:CreateProvisioningTemplate`, `iot:UpdateCACertificate`                                                                                                                              | In `jitp` mode, attempts to create the provisioning template and attaches it to the registered CA. Non-idempotent: a `PUT /v1/dms/{id}` edit retries the creation and lands in `lamassu-dlq` after 3 retries. Idempotent for `none` and `auto` (configuration only). | [DMS registration-mode states](#dms-registration-mode-states) |
  | `EventBindDeviceIdentityKey`                                         | Device               | `IoTCore/Policy`, `IoTCore/ThingGroup`, `IoTCore/Thing` | `iot:CreatePolicy` / `iot:DeletePolicyVersion`, `iot:GetPolicy` / `iot:ListPolicyVersions`, `iot:CreateThingGroup`, `iot:DescribeThing` / `iot:ListThingPrincipals`, `iot:RegisterThing` | In `auto` mode: creates/updates policies, ensures Thing groups, revokes stale principals and provisions the Thing via `iot:RegisterThing`. In `jitp` mode: no AWS calls; AWS runs the JITP template on first connection.                                             | [Thing lifecycle](#thing-lifecycle)                           |
  | `EventUpdateCertificateStatusKey`                                    | Certificate          | `IoTCore/Certificate`                                   | `iot:UpdateCertificate`, `iot:Connect` (data plane)                                                                                                                                      | Maps status to AWS (`ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, `REVOKED`), calls `iot:UpdateCertificate` and forces an MQTT disconnect on revoke.                                                                                                                                         | [Certificate status states](#certificate-status-states)       |
  | `EventUpdateCertificateMetadataKey` / `EventUpdateDeviceMetadataKey` | Certificate / Device | `IoTCore/Certificate`, `IoTCore/Thing`                  | —                                                                                                                                                                                        | Refreshes internal state; the connector ignores events whose CloudEvent `source` matches its own URI to avoid self-triggered loops.                                                                                                                                  | [Device Shadow and automation](#device-shadow-and-automation) |
</div>

CA registration states [#ca-registration-states]

The CA registration flow is driven by the `registration.status` field of the CA's connector metadata:

by the `registration.status` field of the CA's connector metadata:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> NotRegistered: no connector metadata
    NotRegistered --> Requested: admin sets REQUESTED
    Requested --> Registering: connector starts flow
    Registering --> Succeeded: Primary verification certificate or SNI-only direct
    Registering --> Failed: AWS rejects the call
    Failed --> Requested: admin retries
    Succeeded --> Requested: re-registration requested
```

| Transition                           | AWS calls                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NotRegistered` → `Requested`        | none (metadata write only)                                                                                              |
| `Requested` → `Registering`          | `iot:GetRegistrationCode` (Primary Account only)                                                                        |
| `Registering` → `Succeeded`          | `iot:RegisterCACertificate` (Primary: proof-of-possession with an ephemeral key; SNI-only: `CertificateMode: SNI_ONLY`) |
| `Registering` → `Failed`             | failed `iot:RegisterCACertificate`; the error detail is written to the CA's metadata                                    |
| `Failed` / `Succeeded` → `Requested` | none (a new `REQUESTED` write re-runs the flow)                                                                         |

DMS registration-mode states [#dms-registration-mode-states]

The DMS's `registration_mode` determines what the connector does on the AWS side when the DMS is created or fully edited:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> Unconfigured: DMS without connector metadata
    Unconfigured --> None: admin sets the key with mode none
    Unconfigured --> Auto: admin sets the key with mode auto
    Unconfigured --> Jitp: admin sets the key with mode jitp
    None --> Auto: mode switch on DMS edit
    None --> Jitp: mode switch on DMS edit
    Auto --> None: mode switch on DMS edit
    Auto --> Jitp: mode switch on DMS edit
    Jitp --> None: mode switch on DMS edit
    Jitp --> Auto: mode switch on DMS edit
    Jitp --> Jitp: full edit (PUT /v1/dms/{id}) retries template creation
```

| Transition                       | AWS calls                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Unconfigured` → `None` / `Auto` | none (configuration only)                                                                                                                      |
| `None` ↔ `Auto`                  | none (configuration only)                                                                                                                      |
| Any → `Jitp`                     | `iot:CreateProvisioningTemplate` (non-idempotent: it fails when the template already exists; after 3 retries the event lands in `lamassu-dlq`) |
| `Jitp` → `None` / `Auto`         | none (the template stays in the AWS account)                                                                                                   |

Certificate status states [#certificate-status-states]

Certificates holding the connector's metadata key sync their status; certificates provisioned via JITP have no metadata key and stay out of this machine:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> NotSynced: certificate without connector metadata (JITP)
    NotSynced --> Active: status becomes Active
    Active --> Inactive: Revoked + certificateHold
    Active --> Revoked: Revoked (other reasons)
    Inactive --> Active: status becomes Active
    Revoked --> Active: status becomes Active
```

| Transition                                    | AWS calls                                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `NotSynced` → `Active`                        | `iot:UpdateCertificate`                          |
| `Active` → `Inactive`                         | `iot:UpdateCertificate` + forced MQTT disconnect |
| `Active` → `Revoked`                          | `iot:UpdateCertificate` + forced MQTT disconnect |
| `Inactive` / `Revoked` → `Active`             | `iot:UpdateCertificate`                          |
| `RenewalWindow` / `AboutToExpire` / `Expired` | none (these states are not synced to AWS)        |

Thing lifecycle [#thing-lifecycle]

Things only exist under `auto` mode; in `jitp` mode AWS creates the Thing itself when the device first connects. The Thing name is always the device certificate's CN:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> Absent: device not yet enrolled
    Absent --> Provisioned: EventBindDeviceIdentityKey (auto mode)
    Provisioned --> Provisioned: re-enrollment with same CN
```

| Transition                                    | AWS calls                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Absent` → `Provisioned`                      | policies created/updated, Thing groups ensured, `iot:RegisterThing` (creates the Thing, registers the certificate, attaches policies) |
| `Provisioned` → `Provisioned` (re-enrollment) | stale principals marked `REVOKED`, new `iot:RegisterThing` run; the new certificate ARN replaces the old one in Lamassu metadata      |

In `jitp` mode the connector makes no provisioning calls: AWS executes the JITP template on the device's first connection and creates the Thing, registers the certificate and activates it on its own.

CA registration in AWS IoT Core [#ca-registration-in-aws-iot-core]

For devices to authenticate to AWS IoT Core with certificates issued by a Lamassu CA, that CA must first be registered in the AWS account. The connector handles this registration automatically in response to the `EventCreateCAKey`, `EventImportCAKey` and `EventUpdateCAMetadataKey` events, but the operation **only fires when the administrator explicitly requests it** through the CA metadata field.

How to request registration [#how-to-request-registration]

Registration is triggered by setting `registration.status = "REQUESTED"` on the `lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}` key of the CA's metadata. This can be done from the Lamassu console in the CA management section or through the API.

Once the event is received, the connector attempts to register the CA in AWS and updates the `registration.status` field in the CA's metadata with the result: `"SUCCEEDED"` if registration was successful, or `"FAILED"` with an error message otherwise. The process is asynchronous, so you must periodically check the metadata status until the operation completes.

Primary Account [#primary-account]

When the `primary_account` parameter is `true`, the connector runs the full registration flow with proof-of-possession of the private key:

1. It calls `iot:GetRegistrationCode` to obtain AWS's verification code.
2. The connector internally generates an ephemeral RSA-2048 key pair and builds a CSR whose Common Name is exactly that registration code. It then calls Lamassu's signing service so the registered CA issues a real X.509 verification certificate signing that CSR. The ephemeral private key is used only for this purpose and is neither stored nor sent to AWS.
3. It sends the CA (in PEM) and the verification certificate to AWS via `iot:RegisterCACertificate`, enabling registration with `AllowAutoRegistration: true`.

Only one account can own a CA in a given AWS region. If the CA is already registered with the same serial number, the connector silently skips the step.

The tags AWS IoT Core applies to the registered CA certificate are `LMS.CA.ID`, `LMS.CA.SN` and `LMS.CA.CN`.

Secondary Account (SNI-only) [#secondary-account-sni-only]

When `primary_account` is `false`, the connector registers the CA using `CertificateMode: SNI_ONLY`. This mode requires no verification code or access to the CA's private key, so it is the right choice when the CA is managed from another AWS account or when the administrator does not hold the private key. It is the usual method to register the same CA in several AWS accounts simultaneously.

DMS configuration [#dms-configuration]

Each DMS participating in the AWS IoT Core integration must have the metadata key `lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}` configured. The most important field of that configuration is `registration_mode`, which determines how devices are provisioned in AWS.

There are three registration modes, and the choice among them depends on the fleet's provisioning strategy.

none mode [#none-mode]

In this mode the connector **creates no Things, groups or policies** in AWS IoT Core. It only syncs certificate status (active, revoked, suspended) as it changes in Lamassu. It is the right mode when Thing provisioning in AWS is managed by an external system and Lamassu only needs to keep certificate status up to date.

auto mode [#auto-mode]

`auto` mode delegates full device provisioning in AWS to Lamassu at enrollment time. When the device successfully completes its EST enrollment and Lamassu emits the `EventBindDeviceIdentityKey` event, the connector automatically executes the following sequence:

1. Creates or updates the IoT policies configured in the DMS.
2. Creates the root group `LAMASSU` in the AWS account (if it does not exist) and the child groups configured in the DMS as subgroups of `LAMASSU`. If the groups already exist, the `ResourceAlreadyExistsException` error is ignored, making the operation idempotent.
3. If the Thing already existed in AWS IoT Core, the connector iterates all certificates (principals) currently attached to that Thing and marks them as `REVOKED` in AWS, ensuring previous certificates cannot keep being used to authenticate.
4. Calls `iot:RegisterThing` with a CloudFormation-style provisioning template that creates the Thing, registers the device's certificate (PEM of the device certificate and of the issuing CA certificate) and attaches the configured policies.

Once provisioning completes, the connector stores the resulting certificate's ARN in the Lamassu certificate's metadata under the key `lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}` and marks the device as `Registered: true` in Device Manager.

**The Thing name in AWS is the Common Name (CN) of the device's certificate.** This convention is fundamental for the firmware developer: the `/CN=` value the device includes in its CSR when enrolling becomes the ThingName it must identify itself with in all MQTT operations against AWS IoT Core.

jitp mode [#jitp-mode]

Just-In-Time Provisioning (JITP) mode delegates provisioning to AWS instead of the connector doing it directly. When the connector detects the DMS is in `jitp` mode, it creates a JITP provisioning template in AWS IoT Core and attaches it to the registered CA certificate. The connector attempts to create this template when the DMS is created and again on every full DMS edit (`PUT /v1/dms/{id}`) — not at device enrollment time. The attempt is not idempotent: when a template named after the DMS ID already exists, the creation call fails, the event is retried three times and finally lands in the `lamassu-dlq` poison queue (see [Troubleshooting](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/integrations/aws-iot-core#troubleshooting)). The template is created once; later DMS edits never update its content. A DMS update that omits `metadata` or sends `null` keeps the stored metadata, so the connector key `lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}` remains present and the attempt is still triggered. A body that supplies a `metadata` object replaces the stored metadata entirely: if that object does not carry the connector key, the key is dropped and the connector silently skips the DMS's future events. Once the template is attached, when a device with a certificate issued by that CA connects to AWS IoT Core for the first time, AWS executes the template automatically: it creates the Thing, registers the certificate and activates it.

<Callout type="warn" title="Editing a DMS in JITP mode does not update the AWS template">
  The connector creates the template, named after the DMS ID, only once. Each later edit of the DMS that keeps the connector key tries to create it again and fails, because the connector does not update existing templates. Later changes to `jitp_config.provisioning_role_arn`, `jitp_config.enable_template` or to the groups and policies the template references must be applied by hand in AWS IoT Core.

  The failed event is retried and ends in `lamassu-dlq`. Groups and policies are registered before the failure, but the assignment of the template to the registered CA, the write-back of the ARN to the DMS and the shadow update when `ManagedCAs` changes are skipped.
</Callout>

The Thing name in the JITP template is derived from `AWS::IoT::Certificate::CommonName`, which corresponds to the device certificate's CN — the same convention as `auto` mode.

This mode requires the `jitp_config.provisioning_role_arn` field to be configured with the ARN of an IAM role AWS IoT Core can assume to execute the template. If not configured, the connector uses the default `arn:aws:iam::{account}:role/JITPRole` and logs a warning. The administrator must ensure that role exists in the account and has the necessary permissions before enabling JITP mode.

Device provisioning (automatic mode) [#device-provisioning-automatic-mode]

For the firmware developer, `auto` mode is transparent: the device performs its EST enrollment as usual and, as a side effect, it is provisioned in AWS IoT Core with no additional step.

The full flow from the device's perspective is:

```bash
# 1. The device generates its private key and CSR with the CN that will be its ThingName
openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out device.key
openssl req -new -key device.key -sha256 -out device.csr \
  -subj "/CN=my-device-001/O=Acme/OU=IoT"

# 2. The device enrolls in Lamassu via EST
openssl req -in device.csr -outform DER | base64 -w 0 > device.csr.b64
curl -s --cacert lamassu-trust.pem \
  --cert bootstrap.crt --key bootstrap.key \
  -H "Content-Type: application/pkcs10" \
  --data-binary "@device.csr.b64" \
  "https://<EST_HOST>/.well-known/est/<DMS_ID>/simpleenroll" \
  -o enroll.b64

# 3. The device extracts its certificate
base64 -d -i enroll.b64 | openssl pkcs7 -inform DER -print_certs -out device.crt

# From this point on, the connector automatically creates the Thing "my-device-001"
# in AWS IoT Core. The device can connect to AWS with the same certificate.
```

Once the connector completes provisioning, the device can connect to the AWS IoT Core MQTT endpoint using its private key and the certificate issued by Lamassu. The ThingName it must identify itself with in AWS is exactly the certificate's CN.

Device provisioning (JITP mode) [#device-provisioning-jitp-mode]

In JITP mode the device also performs its EST enrollment conventionally and obtains its certificate from Lamassu. The difference is that AWS IoT Core does not know the device until it attempts its first connection.

When the device establishes its first MQTT connection to AWS IoT Core presenting the Lamassu-issued certificate, AWS detects that the certificate belongs to a CA registered with a JITP template, executes that template and creates the Thing automatically. The initial connection may fail or be delayed while the template runs; firmware must be prepared to retry the connection.

For the JITP flow to work correctly:

* The CA must be registered in AWS in Primary Account mode (SNI-only mode does not support JITP).
* The IAM role configured in `jitp_config.provisioning_role_arn` must exist and have permissions to create Things, register certificates and attach policies in the AWS account.
* The device must present both its certificate and the issuing CA's certificate in the TLS handshake with AWS IoT Core.

Certificates provisioned via JITP **do not have the connector's metadata key** (`lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}`) in Lamassu. As a consequence, status changes of those certificates in Lamassu are not automatically synced to AWS through the state synchronization mechanism described in the next section.

Certificate status synchronization [#certificate-status-synchronization]

The connector listens for the `EventUpdateCertificateStatusKey` event and, when a certificate holding the connector's metadata key changes status in Lamassu, replicates that change in AWS IoT Core. The following table shows the status mapping:

| Status in Lamassu | Revocation reason | Status in AWS IoT Core |
| ----------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------- |
| `Active`          | None              | `ACTIVE`               |
| `Revoked`         | `certificateHold` | `INACTIVE`             |
| `Revoked`         | Any other reason  | `REVOKED`              |

Only the `Active` and `Revoked` states produce a call to `iot:UpdateCertificate`. The other lifecycle states of Lamassu (`RenewalWindow`, `AboutToExpire`, `Expired`) are not synced to AWS IoT Core; the certificate status in AWS remains unchanged until the status in Lamassu becomes `Active` or `Revoked`.

Forced disconnect on revocation [#forced-disconnect-on-revocation]

When the connector marks a certificate as `REVOKED` or `INACTIVE` in AWS, it additionally performs a forced disconnect of the device. To do so it opens an MQTT connection over WebSocket (with SigV4 authentication using the connector's credentials) to the AWS IoT Core data endpoint, using the certificate's CN as the MQTT client identifier, and closes it immediately. This terminates any active MQTT session the device may have at that moment.

This forced disconnect happens at the moment Lamassu records the status change. If the device tries to reconnect after the disconnect, AWS IoT Core will reject the connection because the certificate is already listed as `REVOKED` or `INACTIVE`.

Certificates provisioned in JITP mode do not have this automatic sync, since they lack the connector's metadata key.

Device Shadow and automation [#device-shadow-and-automation]

The connector can write to the AWS IoT Core Device Shadow to send action signals to the device firmware. This feature is enabled per DMS with `shadow_config.enable: true`.

If `shadow_config.shadow_name` holds a value, the connector uses a Named Shadow with that name; otherwise it uses the Classic Shadow (the Thing's default shadow).

What the connector writes to the shadow [#what-the-connector-writes-to-the-shadow]

The connector writes to the `desired.identity_actions` field of the shadow document. Each entry contains a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. The device firmware must read this field and act accordingly.

There are two action types:

**`UPDATE_CERTIFICATE`**: written when a certificate's preventive renewal window activates — that is, when the `triggered` field of the preventive renewal delta flips from `false` to `true`. This action tells the device it must start the re-enrollment process to renew its certificate before it expires.

**`UPDATE_TRUST_ANCHOR_LIST`**: written to all devices of a DMS when the DMS's `ManagedCAs` list changes. This action tells the device it must update its trusted CA store.

The shadow write process consists of reading the current shadow (`iotdata:GetThingShadow`), merging the new actions with the existing ones and writing the result (`iotdata:UpdateThingShadow`). If the shadow does not exist, the connector creates it. After a successful write, the list of pending actions in the device's metadata in Lamassu is cleared.

```json
{
  "state": {
    "desired": {
      "identity_actions": {
        "UPDATE_CERTIFICATE": 1716300000000,
        "UPDATE_TRUST_ANCHOR_LIST": 1716299000000
      }
    }
  }
}
```

AWS IoT policies [#aws-iot-policies]

The connector creates and attaches the policies configured in the DMS. A typical policy for a device using MQTT and the Device Shadow has this structure:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "iot:Connect"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:iot:<AWS_REGION>:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:client/${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "iot:Publish"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:iot:<AWS_REGION>:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:topic/$aws/things/${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}",
        "arn:aws:iot:<AWS_REGION>:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:topic/$aws/things/${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}/shadow/[name/${ShadowName}/]*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "iot:Subscribe"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:iot:<AWS_REGION>:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:topicfilter/$aws/things/${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}",
        "arn:aws:iot:<AWS_REGION>:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:topicfilter/$aws/things/${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}/shadow/[name/${ShadowName}/]*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "iot:Receive"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:iot:<AWS_REGION>:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:topic/$aws/things/${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}",
        "arn:aws:iot:<AWS_REGION>:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:topic/$aws/things/${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}/shadow/[name/${ShadowName}/]*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

In the policy above, the `<AWS_REGION>` and `<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>` placeholders must be replaced with the AWS region and the twelve-digit account identifier of the target account before applying the policy. The `${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}` variable automatically limits each permission to the Thing the device is connected as, following the principle of least privilege. The `${ShadowName}` variable in the shadow ARNs is a placeholder that must be replaced with the `shadow_config.shadow_name` value configured in the DMS; if the Classic Shadow is used, it can be simplified by removing the `name/${ShadowName}/` segment. AWS IoT policies do not support regex alternation; the `[name/${ShadowName}/]*` notation represents the optionality of that segment within ARN syntax constraints.

The first statement lets the device connect using its ThingName as the MQTT identifier. The second authorizes publishing to the Thing's generic MQTT topic and to the shadow topics, needed so the device can update its reported state. The last two statements grant subscribe and receive permissions over the same topics, letting the device receive shadow updates (for example, the `UPDATE_CERTIFICATE` and `UPDATE_TRUST_ANCHOR_LIST` actions written by the connector).

Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

**Symptom:** The CA registration stays in `REQUESTED` indefinitely.

**Cause:** The connector is not running or is not subscribed to the event bus. It can also indicate incorrect IAM credentials, insufficient permissions or that the metadata key was written with a wrong `connector_id`.

**Resolution:** Verify the connector process is active and the logs show no AWS communication errors. Check the metadata field was written under the exact key `lamassu.io/iot/{connector_id}`. If the error persists, the connector will update the status to `FAILED` with a descriptive message in the CA metadata.

***

**Symptom:** A certificate's status is not synced to AWS after a revocation.

**Cause:** Most commonly the certificate was provisioned in JITP mode. JITP certificates lack the connector's metadata key and are outside the state synchronization mechanism. If the DMS is in `auto` mode, it may indicate the initial provisioning did not complete correctly and the AWS ARN was not stored in the certificate metadata.

**Resolution:** For JITP certificates, migrate the DMS to `auto` mode and re-provision the affected devices. For `auto` mode certificates, verify the certificate has the AWS ARN stored in its metadata; if not, repeat the provisioning.

***

**Symptom:** The forced disconnect does not terminate the device's MQTT session after revocation.

**Cause:** The device uses an MQTT client ID different from the certificate's CN. The forced disconnect opens a connection using the CN as client ID; if the firmware uses another identifier, the disconnect does not affect that session.

**Resolution:** Make sure the firmware uses exactly the certificate's CN as the MQTT client identifier. That CN matches the ThingName in AWS IoT Core.

***

**Symptom:** The device receives `CLIENT_ID_REJECTED` when connecting to AWS IoT Core.

**Cause:** The MQTT client ID does not match the ThingName, which is always the CN of the certificate issued by Lamassu.

**Resolution:** Verify the firmware uses exactly the value of the CN field included in the enrollment CSR as the MQTT client identifier.

***

**Symptom:** The device's first MQTT connection in JITP mode fails or times out.

**Cause:** This is expected behavior while AWS executes the JITP template on the device's first connection.

**Resolution:** Firmware must implement retries with exponential backoff for the first connection. If the failure persists beyond a few minutes, verify the IAM role configured in `jitp_config.provisioning_role_arn` exists in the account and has permissions to create Things, register certificates and attach policies.

***

**Symptom:** The Device Shadow is not updated when it should be.

**Cause:** The shadow feature is disabled in the DMS configuration, the connector's credentials lack IoT data-plane permissions, or the firmware reads a different shadow than the configured one.

**Resolution:** Check that `shadow_config.enable` is `true` in the connector metadata for the corresponding DMS. If a Named Shadow is used, verify `shadow_config.shadow_name` holds the correct name and that the firmware reads that Named Shadow and not the Classic Shadow. Confirm the connector's credentials have `iotdata:GetThingShadow` and `iotdata:UpdateThingShadow` permissions.

***

**Symptom:** After editing a DMS in `jitp` mode, DMS update messages appear in `lamassu-dlq`, or JITP configuration changes have no effect in AWS.

**Cause:** Every full DMS edit (`PUT /v1/dms/{id}`) triggers a `CreateProvisioningTemplate` attempt for the template named after the DMS ID, and the call is not idempotent: when the template already exists, it fails, the event is retried three times and finally lands in `lamassu-dlq`. The connector’s later steps are skipped.

**Resolution:** Check that the template named with the DMS ID exists in AWS IoT Core and that JITP enrollment works. If the JITP configuration was changed, apply it by hand to the AWS template.

  <Card title="Certificate management" href="/docs/platform/pki/certificates" />

# IoT Fleets (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/iot-fleets/overview)



IoT Fleets applies PKI to the device lifecycle: registration, obtaining an identity, renewal and retirement. It is intended for those who administer a device population and those who integrate its enrollment client or the system that accepts it.

Start here [#start-here]

Follow [Enroll and connect your first device](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/quickstarts/enroll-device) to prepare a DMS, obtain the identity from the client and demonstrate an mTLS connection. The automatic path includes initial trust, a CSR and result checks.

To start with an existing certificate, use [Register a device manually](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/quickstarts/register-device). You can then prepare enrollment and renewal for the next device.

Devices and identities [#devices-and-identities]

| Resource     | What it represents                                                                 |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Device**   | An inventory entry with an identifier, owning DMS and classification.              |
| **Identity** | The device's association with its certificates: an active version and a history.   |
| **DMS**      | The service that configures admission, enrollment, renewal and trust distribution. |
| **Fleet**    | The population you operate, represented through devices, DMSs, tags and metadata.  |

Each device has an owning DMS. You can organize a population through several DMSs when it needs different policies, and use tags to classify it. “Fleet” describes that operational context; the resources you create and query are DMSs and devices.

[Device management](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/device-management) covers states, certificate history and identity actions. During renewal, retain the relationship with the device and check which certificate becomes the current identity.

Enrollment with PKI [#enrollment-with-pki]

This section connects PKI rules to the device client. Preparation follows this order:

1. **CA and profile:** prepare the issuer and certificate rules in [PKI](/docs/platform/pki/overview).
2. **DMS policy:** define how the device is admitted, how requests authenticate and which trust is distributed.
3. **Client:** prepare the initial credential, server trust, and key generation or custody.
4. **Result:** request the certificate, install it and check its association with the device.
5. **Continuity:** configure renewal, successor installation and recovery according to DMS policy.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Configure the DMS" description="Prepare the CA, admission, authentication and renewal rules." href="/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/dms" />

  <Card title="Integrate the EST client" description="Review the device endpoints, formats and checks." href="/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/est-client" />
</Cards>

Integrations [#integrations]

An issued identity needs a consumer that trusts its issuer, validates the certificate and grants the device permissions. Prepare both the device's trust in the server and the server's trust in the device.

The [AWS IoT Core guide](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/integrations/aws-iot-core) explains how to use the identity in that destination. Provisioning in Lamassu and provisioning in the destination are separate decisions; review the conditions of the chosen mode before expecting state synchronization.

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Software updates [#software-updates]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Once devices hold an identity, Lamassu Updates delivers firmware and software to them over the air. You publish a pack, choose the devices or groups that receive it and watch the rollout; devices install it with SWUpdate, and packages can be signed and encrypted.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Cards>
    <Card title="Lamassu Updates" description="Understand the service, its two backends and the update lifecycle." href="/docs/platform/updates/overview" />

    <Card title="Publish and roll out an update" description="Create a pack, build the package and launch it to a group of devices." href="/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out" />
  </Cards>
</div>

Who prepares each part [#who-prepares-each-part]

| Participant                | Responsibility                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| PKI administrator          | CA, issuance profile, chain and revocation publication.                  |
| Provisioning administrator | DMS, admission, authentication per operation and inventory.              |
| Device integrator          | Initial credential, key, EST client, trust and certificate installation. |
| Consumer integrator        | Trusted issuers, validation and device permissions in the destination.   |

[Permissions](/docs/platform/administration/access-control) and [audit](/docs/platform/administration/audit-logs) are shared with the rest of Platform. Prepare installation and instance connectivity in [Deployment](/docs/deployment/overview).


# Enroll and connect your first device (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/iot-fleets/quickstarts/enroll-device)



Prepare an evaluation DMS, enroll `est-device-001` from the client and use its identity with a local consumer that requires a certificate. The path connects administrator policy to the material the device actually installs.

Before you begin [#before-you-begin]

* A Lamassu instance accessible through HTTPS and permissions for CAs, profiles, DMSs and reading devices/certificates.
* Bash, OpenSSL 3.x, curl with `--fail-with-body` and two terminals on your computer. Work in a new directory with restricted access.
* An active root CA that issues directly, with an available key and sufficient validity. Follow [Create your first CA](/docs/platform/pki/quickstarts/create-certificate-authority). Save its verified public certificate as `device-root.pem`.
* Available global identifier `est-device-001`. This path uses automatic registration: do not create the device in the console first.
* The approved root for Lamassu HTTPS in `est-trust.pem`, obtained through an independent channel. It can differ from the device CA; prepare networking/TLS in [Deployment](/docs/deployment/self-hosted/networking).

Prepare the bootstrap credential [#prepare-the-bootstrap-credential]

Issue a bootstrap leaf certificate with `CN=est-device-001`, its own key and Client Authentication use. Follow [Issue and verify a certificate](/docs/platform/pki/quickstarts/issue-certificate), changing its CN and saving the result as `bootstrap.crt` and `bootstrap.key`. Choose validity that covers this test and check the pair and chain.

The same root CA can issue it for this isolated evaluation. The operational identity will have a different key and certificate. The matching CN makes the example easier to read; initial certificate authentication does not itself bind the bootstrap CN to the requested ID. Review [admission](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/bootstrap-identity) before applying the policy to a population.

Configure the evaluation DMS [#configure-the-evaluation-dms]

Create an explicit leaf profile compatible with EC P-256, with **Honor Subject**, CN from the CSR, **Digital Signature**, **Client Authentication** and **1 hour** validity within the root's validity. Do not enable CA signing. Rules and precedence are explained in [Profiles](/docs/platform/pki/certificate-profiles).

Create the `Acme EST Evaluation` DMS with this configuration:

| Setting                                               | Evaluation value                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Enrollment CA                                         | Issuing root from `device-root.pem`.                                                                   |
| Issuance profile                                      | The 1-hour leaf profile you just prepared.                                                             |
| Protocol / Registration Mode                          | `EST_RFC7030` / `JITP`.                                                                                |
| Verify CSR Signature                                  | Enabled.                                                                                               |
| Enable Replaceable Enrollment                         | Disabled; the ID must be new.                                                                          |
| Initial authentication                                | `CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`; Validation CAs includes the direct bootstrap issuer; no expired certificates.    |
| Renewal authentication                                | `CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`, configured in the independent re-enrollment block.                               |
| Re-enrollment Validation CAs / Enable Expired Renewal | Not needed for this direct issuance; the Enrollment CA is always trusted for re-enrollment / disabled. |
| Re-enrollment Delta                                   | 1 hour.                                                                                                |
| Preventive / Critical Delta                           | 30 minutes / 10 minutes.                                                                               |
| Revoke on Re-enrollment                               | Disabled to test the successor before retiring the previous identity.                                  |
| ServerKeyGen                                          | Disabled; the operational key is generated in the client.                                              |
| CA Distribution                                       | Include Enrollment CA enabled; Include Lamassu System CA disabled.                                     |

Equal duration and window allow immediate renewal testing. These are evaluation values; size production settings according to connectivity and recovery times. Save, reread both authentication blocks and retain the DMS ID. The console exposes independent editors for the enrollment and re-enrollment authentication; the [DMS guide](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/dms) describes their fields, and you can also check the resource through the [DMS API](/docs/api-reference/dms-manager).

Prepare the client and check cacerts [#prepare-the-client-and-check-cacerts]

Place the four trust and bootstrap files in the new directory. Replace the URL with your installation's URL:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
EST_BASE='https://lamassu.example.com/.well-known/est/REPLACE_DMS_ID'
```

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --show-error --silent --max-time 30 \
  --cacert est-trust.pem \
  --dump-header cacerts.headers --output cacerts.b64 \
  "$EST_BASE/cacerts"
openssl base64 -d -in cacerts.b64 -out cacerts.p7b
openssl pkcs7 -inform DER -in cacerts.p7b -print_certs -quiet -out cacerts.pem
openssl crl2pkcs7 -nocrl -certfile cacerts.pem | openssl pkcs7 -print_certs -noout
```

The download must succeed and contain the expected enrollment root. Compare its fingerprint with `device-root.pem`. This check does not turn the response into initial trust or prove that you can issue.

Enroll the device [#enroll-the-device]

Generate a new key and CSR with the selected identifier:

```bash
test ! -e device.key
openssl genpkey -algorithm EC -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -out device.key
openssl req -new -sha256 -key device.key -subj '/CN=est-device-001' -out device.csr
openssl req -in device.csr -verify -noout
openssl req -in device.csr -outform DER -out device.csr.der
openssl base64 -A -in device.csr.der -out device.csr.b64
```

Request the identity with the bootstrap credential and extract the certificate from the default response:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --show-error --silent --max-time 30 \
  --cacert est-trust.pem --cert bootstrap.crt --key bootstrap.key \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/pkcs10' \
  --data-binary @device.csr.b64 \
  --dump-header enroll.headers --output enroll.b64 \
  "$EST_BASE/simpleenroll"
openssl base64 -d -in enroll.b64 -out enroll.p7b
openssl pkcs7 -inform DER -in enroll.p7b -print_certs -quiet -out device.crt
```

If curl fails, use [Troubleshooting](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/troubleshooting) with the saved body. Do not convert it or repeat the request without querying inventory: a timeout or error can follow persisted issuance.

Verify the obtained identity [#verify-the-obtained-identity]

```bash
openssl verify -CAfile device-root.pem -purpose sslclient device.crt
openssl x509 -in device.crt -noout -subject -issuer -serial -dates -text
openssl x509 -in device.crt -pubkey -noout > certificate-public.pem
openssl pkey -pubin -in certificate-public.pem -outform DER -out certificate-public.der
openssl pkey -in device.key -pubout -outform DER -out key-public.der
cmp certificate-public.der key-public.der
```

Expect `device.crt: OK` and exit code 0 from `cmp`. Check the CN, serial, dates, Digital Signature and Client Authentication. The certificate must be a leaf: it must not declare `CA:TRUE` or Certificate Sign use. Check that its validity matches the one-hour profile.

In Lamassu, open `est-device-001`. It must be created with the intended owning DMS, a current identity and the received certificate in its history. Compare the local serial with the slot; thresholds can show a renewal state rather than simply Active.

Demonstrate an mTLS connection [#demonstrate-an-mtls-connection]

In a second terminal, enter the same directory and run `umask 077`. Create a local server certificate and start a test consumer. This server trusts `device-root.pem` and requires a valid client identity:

```bash
test ! -e consumer.key
openssl req -new -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 \
  -noenc -days 1 -subj '/CN=localhost' \
  -addext 'subjectAltName=DNS:localhost' \
  -addext 'basicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE' \
  -addext 'keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature' \
  -addext 'extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth' \
  -keyout consumer.key -out consumer.crt
openssl s_server -accept 127.0.0.1:8443 -cert consumer.crt -key consumer.key \
  -CAfile device-root.pem -Verify 2 -verify_return_error -purpose sslclient -www
```

Leave it running. In the first terminal, connect using the obtained identity:

```bash
curl --fail --show-error --silent --max-time 10 \
  --cacert consumer.crt --cert device.crt --key device.key \
  --output mtls-result.html --write-out '%{http_code}\n' \
  https://localhost:8443/
```

Expect HTTP `200`. The client's trust in this local server is its self-signed `consumer.crt`; the server verifies the device against `device-root.pem`. The HTML file displays OpenSSL diagnostic information.

With the same server still running, test that a request without a client certificate is rejected:

```bash
if curl --fail --show-error --silent --max-time 10 \
  --cacert consumer.crt --output /dev/null https://localhost:8443/; then
  printf '%s\n' 'ERROR: consumer accepted a request without a client certificate' >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

Rejection must correspond to a missing certificate at the server, not a stopped server. Stop the consumer with Ctrl+C after the test. This exercise demonstrates TLS authentication and key possession; your application must also define authorization and revocation consumption. Server options are described in [openssl-s\_server](https://docs.openssl.org/3.6/man1/openssl-s_server/).

Result and continuity [#result-and-continuity]

| Check        | Expected result                                                        |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Registration | ID created automatically and correct DMS.                              |
| Certificate  | CN, profile, serial and key verified.                                  |
| Inventory    | Received serial visible as the current identity and in history.        |
| Consumer     | mTLS responds 200 with the identity and rejects a missing certificate. |

Continue with [Renewal and recovery](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/enrollment/renewal-and-recovery) to request a successor pair within the window, install it and repeat the mTLS check. The consumer must use the new files in that test. After checking the successor, retire the previous certificate according to PKI policy; the example does not revoke it automatically.

[Devices and identities](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/device-management) explains retirement and the limits of historical revocation. For a real destination, prepare consumer trust, validation and permissions; [AWS IoT Core](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/integrations/aws-iot-core) is an available integration.


# Register a device manually (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/iot-fleets/quickstarts/register-device)



This path is intended for those starting to administer device identities. You will register `device-001` and assign an existing certificate to check the relationship between device, DMS and identity history.

Assignment updates Lamassu's inventory. Install the key and certificate separately on the device; check the connection to a consumer in that destination's integration.

Before you begin [#before-you-begin]

* An accessible instance and permission to administer DMSs, devices and certificate associations.
* An active CA with an available key. If one does not exist yet, follow [Create your first CA](/docs/platform/pki/quickstarts/create-certificate-authority).
* An active end-entity certificate from that CA whose `Common Name` is exactly `device-001`, together with its private key. Follow [Issue and verify a certificate](/docs/platform/pki/quickstarts/issue-certificate) to obtain and check both.
* The identifier `device-001` available in the inventory. If you already used it, choose another and issue the certificate with that same `Common Name`.

Prepare the DMS [#prepare-the-dms]

A DMS must exist before registering the device. If you already have a suitable one, check its CA and note its identifier; to create one:

1. Open the DMS inventory and its creation action. Assign a recognizable name, such as `Acme Evaluation DMS`.
2. In **Enrollment CA**, select the CA that issued `device.crt`.
3. In **Registration Mode**, select `PRE_REGISTRATION` for the path that starts with explicit registration.
4. In the authentication section, enable **Require client certificate** and leave **Call external webhook** off. Under **Require client certificate**, add the CA whose initial certificates you will accept to **Validation CAs**; for this evaluation, it can be the same CA.
