  4. React to a device finishing [#4-react-to-a-device-finishing]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Every state change WFX reports runs the same logic. This is what makes automatic batching, the canary gate and the error threshold work.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  On **every** event the service updates the device's update history and writes the event to the device's metadata in Lamassu. Then, only if the state is a terminal one of the workflow, it runs these checks in order, and the first one that applies decides what happens:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | # | Check                                                                                       | If it applies                                                                                  |
  | - | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | 1 | Is the state terminal in the workflow?                                                      | If not, nothing more happens                                                                   |
  | 2 | (always)                                                                                    | Mark the device's assignment `completed` or `failed`. On success, record the installed version |
  | 3 | Did the canary device fail?                                                                 | Pause the launch. Resume to retry                                                              |
  | 4 | Is the launch paused, cancelled or completed?                                               | Stop: no further batches                                                                       |
  | 5 | Is `error_threshold` set, and have failures reached that share of all devices (rounded up)? | Cancel the launch. Pending devices are not sent                                                |
  | 6 | Is nothing pending and nothing active?                                                      | Mark the launch `completed`                                                                    |
  | 7 | Is `auto` off, or is nothing left to send?                                                  | Wait for the operator's next `rollout` call, or for the devices still in flight                |
  | 8 | Did at least `approval_threshold` of this batch succeed? (0 or 100 or more means all of it) | Dispatch the next batch. Otherwise wait for more results                                       |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Only devices dispatched in the current batch count toward its approval: a straggler from an earlier batch never does. The checks move the launch between these states:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> running: launch created
    running --> paused: operator pauses, or the canary fails
    paused --> running: resume
    running --> cancelled: operator cancels, or error_threshold reached
    paused --> cancelled: operator cancels
    running --> completed: nothing pending and nothing active, or operator completes
    paused --> completed: operator completes
    completed --> running: retry-failed
    cancelled --> running: retry-failed
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A new launch is stored with an empty status, which means `running`. Resuming after a failed canary re-queues the canary so it is tried again. Cancelling stops further batches but does not recall jobs that are already running on devices.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  5. Build a per-device encrypted pack [#5-build-a-per-device-encrypted-pack]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Each device gets its own package, encrypted with its own key. The build first resolves every device's key, then builds. A device without a key is skipped, and a launch on a pack with skipped devices is refused.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  sequenceDiagram
    actor Op as Operator
    participant API as Updates API
    participant SYM as SymKMS
    participant DMS as Lamassu Device Manager
    participant SWG as swugenerator

    loop each device
      Op->>SYM: POST /symkms/v1/ create key
      Op->>SYM: POST /symkms/v1/inventory/{device}/keys/{key} {purpose: firmware-encryption}
    end
    Op->>API: POST .../swu {encryption_alg_name, selected_artifact_ids}
    API->>DMS: list the group's devices
    Note over API: build fails if the group has no devices, or the sw-description marks no file encrypted = true
    par each device, concurrently
      API->>SYM: GET /symkms/v1/inventory/{device}/key
    end
    Note over API: build fails if no device has a key
    par each device with a key, concurrently
      API->>SWG: build a .swu encrypted with that key
    end
    API->>API: record built_device_count, total_device_count, uncovered_devices
    API-->>Op: 200
    Note over Op,API: Launch creation returns 400 while uncovered_devices is not empty
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `uncovered_devices` lists devices without a key and also devices whose own build failed. A build where no device got a package leaves the pack `build_failed`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit mode [#hawkbit-mode]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  6. Build a module and create a pack [#6-build-a-module-and-create-a-pack]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit itself has no notion of a built module, and this service links only built modules into a hawkBit distribution set. A set is never built directly: `POST .../swu` and `.../package` answer `501` in this mode. The module is built first, in the catalog, and the pack is created from it. The diagram shows the `swu-build` intent.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  sequenceDiagram
    actor Op as Operator
    participant API as Updates API
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant SWG as swugenerator
    participant HB as hawkBit

    Op->>API: POST /softwaremodules {type, name, version, delivery_intent}
    API->>HB: create software module
    API-->>Op: module id
    Op->>API: POST /softwaremodules/by-id/{id}/artifacts (file)
    API->>HB: upload the artifact to the module
    Op->>API: POST /softwaremodules/by-id/{id}/descriptor (sw-description)
    API->>DB: store the sw-description
    Op->>API: POST /softwaremodules/by-id/{id}/build
    API->>HB: read the module's input files
    API->>SWG: build the .swu
    SWG-->>API: .swu file
    API->>HB: upload the .swu, then remove the module's input artifacts
    API-->>Op: module built
    Op->>API: POST /groups/{g}/distribution-sets {modules: [{source_module_id}]}
    API->>HB: create the distribution set linking the built module
    API->>HB: tag it with the group
    opt the modules were signed
      API->>DB: store the signed set manifest
    end
    API-->>Op: 201 pack (already built)
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The other delivery intents skip steps: `swu-prebuilt` only uploads the finished `.swu`, which is what builds the module, and `raw` only encrypts or signs the files, with no swugenerator and no sw-description (signing adds a `.sha256` checksum document and its detached signature as extra artifacts). A build can sign through the KMS and encrypt with a shared SymKMS key. Per-device encryption is refused in hawkBit mode. A linked module is frozen: to change it, edit and build it in the catalog, then link it again.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  7. Launch and device update [#7-launch-and-device-update]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The device talks to hawkBit, not to this service. The service reads progress back from hawkBit whenever it is asked.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  sequenceDiagram
    actor Op as Operator
    participant API as Updates API
    participant DMS as Lamassu Device Manager
    participant HB as hawkBit
    participant Dev as Device (SWUpdate suricatta)

    Op->>API: POST /groups/{g}/launch {pack, strategy}
    API->>DMS: list the devices of the group
    API->>HB: create the missing targets and tag them group:{g}
    API->>API: check the canary, the pack's group and the preconditions
    API->>HB: create a rollout (optional canary group, then batches, then the rest)
    API-->>Op: 201 launch_id, never_seen_devices
    Op->>API: POST .../rollout
    API->>HB: start the rollout, or release the next group
    Dev->>HB: DDI poll, authenticated per the tenant's settings
    HB-->>Dev: deploymentBase with the module's artifact
    Dev->>HB: download the .swu
    Dev->>HB: feedback proceeding, then closed with result success
    HB->>HB: rollout group counters, success and error conditions
    Op->>API: GET /groups/{g}/launch
    API->>HB: read the rollout and its groups
    API-->>Op: status and counters
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A canary group exists only when `test_device_id` is given. hawkBit decides when a group succeeds and the next group starts, using the approval and error thresholds the service gave it. With `auto` off, hawkBit pauses after each group and the next `rollout` call releases the following one. The launch response also lists `superseded_devices` (devices whose in-flight update the new rollout replaces) and `never_seen_devices` (devices that have never polled, which can stall a group that must reach its success threshold).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `rollout` call depends on the rollout's state:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * A `ready` rollout is started, and nothing happens while its start time is in the future.
  * A paused rollout is resumed only if it is paused between batches. An operator pause needs `resume`, and a rollout stopped by its error threshold cannot be resumed.
  * A running manual rollout releases its next group.
  * An `auto` rollout that is already running is refused with `400`.
  * A second `rollout` on the same launch while one is in progress answers `409`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Device authentication is a hawkBit tenant setting. Target security tokens are off by default. See [Connect a device](/docs/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Next steps [#next-steps]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Cards>
    <Card title="Publish and roll out an update" description="Run flows 1 to 4 end to end." href="/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out" />

    <Card title="Data model" description="The tables behind these flows." href="/docs/platform/updates/data-model" />

    <Card title="Signing and encryption" description="Keys, signatures and the manifest." href="/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption" />
  </Cards>
</div>


# Get started with Lamassu Updates (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/getting-started)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  This guide starts Lamassu Updates (the OTA Update Service) with Docker Compose, in its default native mode, and checks that the API answers. It takes about ten minutes plus the image build. When it works, continue with [Publish and roll out an update](/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Before you begin [#before-you-begin]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * Docker with the Compose plugin.
  * A running Lamassu IoT instance that the containers can reach. The service reads device groups and their devices from its Device Manager (`dms_endpoint`), and signs with its KMS (`kms_endpoint`) only when you ask for signed builds.
  * A checkout of the [`ota` repository](https://github.com/lamassuiot/ota) with the Lamassu `core` and `sdk` modules next to it. `go.mod` replaces `lamassuiot/core` and `lamassuiot/sdk` with local paths, and the Docker build copies them from the **parent directory** of the checkout (`context: ..` in `docker-compose.yml`), so that directory must contain both `ota/` and `lamassuiot/`.
  * Access to the `ghcr.io/lamassuiot/wfx:otaq` image, which the `custom-wfx` service uses.
  * Optional, for [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode): a hawkBit server. Compose builds one from `docker/hawkbit`: hawkBit 1.1.0 plus an S3 artifact plugin, tagged `lamassu/hawkbit-update-server:1.1.0-s3` locally. That image is built locally and not published.
  * Optional, to run the service outside Docker: Go 1.26.2 or newer, and Python 3.8 or newer with the `swugenerator` requirements installed. The Docker image already contains the compiled binary and Python with `swugenerator`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Start the stack [#start-the-stack]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Clone the repository [#clone-the-repository]

      ```bash
      git clone https://github.com/lamassuiot/ota.git
      cd ota
      ```
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Set the host address [#set-the-host-address]

      The `updates` container reaches Lamassu through `host.docker.internal`, which `docker-compose.yml` overrides with `HOST_IP`. On WSL2 the default `host.docker.internal` points at the Docker Desktop gateway, not at the WSL host, so set your own address:

      ```bash
      cp .env.example .env
      HOST_IP=$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')
      sed -i "s/HOST_IP=/HOST_IP=${HOST_IP}/" .env
      ```

      Then check that `dms_endpoint` and `kms_endpoint` in `config-docker.yml` point at your Lamassu API (they default to `http://host.docker.internal:8080/api/...`).
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Create the network and start [#create-the-network-and-start]

      `docker-compose.yml` attaches to an existing network named `ota-net` and refuses to start without it.

      ```bash
      docker network create ota-net
      docker compose up --build
      ```
    </Step>
  </Steps>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Services [#services]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Service            | Host port                            | What it is                                                                        |
  | ------------------ | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `updates`          | `10090`                              | The Updates API, with SymKMS embedded                                             |
  | `custom-wfx`       | `9080` (client), `9081` (management) | WFX, the job server that devices poll in native mode                              |
  | `postgres`         | `5000` (container `5432`)            | Database. `init.sql` creates the `updates` and `hawkbit` databases on first start |
  | `swupdate-device1` | `80`                                 | A sample SWUpdate device client                                                   |
  | `hawkbit`          | `8090`                               | hawkBit server, only for [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode)      |
  | `rustfs`           | `9000` (S3), `9001` (console)        | Local S3 store, only with `--profile s3`                                          |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `docker compose --profile s3 up -d` also starts `rustfs` and `s3-init`, which creates the encrypted bucket `ota-updates` that artifacts, builds and hawkBit's artifact storage can use. Without that profile, and with `config-docker.yml`, artifacts and builds stay on the `update_files` volume.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Verify the API [#verify-the-api]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s localhost:10090/health
  # {"status":"ok"}

  curl -s localhost:10090/updates/v1/capabilities
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The second call reports the active backend and what it supports. In native mode it looks like this (shortened):
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {
    "backend": "native",
    "supported": { "workflows": true, "campaigns": true, "software_module_deliverables": false },
    "unsupported": ["software_module_deliverables", "software_module_replace"]
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `supported` has one entry for each of the 22 capabilities. See [Capabilities](/docs/platform/updates/reference/capabilities) for what each one means.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Run without Docker [#run-without-docker]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Start the monolithic entry point with a config file. It runs the Updates API and SymKMS together.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  OTA_CONFIG_FILE=/path/to/config.yml go run ./cmd/monolithic
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If `OTA_CONFIG_FILE` is not set, the service reads `/etc/lamassuiot/config.yml`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To build `.swu` files outside Docker, install `swugenerator` into the Python environment that the config points at (the image does the same from `swugenerator/requirements.txt`):
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  python3 -m venv .venv
  .venv/bin/pip install -r swugenerator/requirements.txt
  .venv/bin/pip install -e swugenerator
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `config.yml` at the repository root is a starting point for local development, not a ready-made file:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * It needs Postgres (`localhost:5000`) and the WFX management API (`localhost:9081`), which `docker compose up -d postgres custom-wfx` provides.
  * It contains values for one developer machine: absolute `/home/alvaro/...` paths for artifact and SymKMS storage, the signer script and `swugenerator`, and a LAN IP for the Lamassu endpoints. Edit them to paths the service user can create; the service stops at start-up if it cannot create its directories.
  * It stores artifacts and build outputs in the local RustFS bucket (`docker compose --profile s3 up -d`). To use local disk instead, remove the `artifacts:` and `builds:` blocks; when they are absent, artifacts default to `{update_files_base_dir}/artifacts`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Try hawkBit mode [#try-hawkbit-mode]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit mode serves the same API on top of a real hawkBit server. Start hawkBit and Postgres, wait until hawkBit answers, then start the service with the hawkBit config:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  docker compose up -d postgres hawkbit

  until curl -sf -u admin:admin 'http://localhost:8090/rest/v1/targets?limit=1' >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done

  OTA_CONFIG_FILE=./config-hawkbit.yml go run ./cmd/monolithic
  curl -s localhost:10090/updates/v1/capabilities   # "backend":"hawkbit"
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `config-hawkbit.yml` also contains developer-machine paths, in the SWU build settings. A service pointed at a hawkBit with no registered devices builds and launches normally, but nothing downloads the update, because in hawkBit mode devices poll hawkBit directly. Read [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode) before using it.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                                   | Likely cause                                                                                                                                            |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `docker compose up` fails on the network                                  | `ota-net` does not exist. Run `docker network create ota-net`                                                                                           |
  | The `updates` container cannot reach Lamassu                              | `HOST_IP` is empty in `.env`, or `dms_endpoint` in `config-docker.yml` points at an address the container cannot reach                                  |
  | `docker compose up --build` fails while copying `lamassuiot/core`         | The build context (the parent of `ota/`) does not contain `lamassuiot/`                                                                                 |
  | The service exits at start-up when run on the host                        | A directory in the config (`update_files_base_dir`, `sym_keys_dir`) cannot be created, or Postgres or WFX is not reachable at the addresses in the file |
  | `capabilities` answers but device groups fail with a Device Manager error | `dms_endpoint` is wrong. The Updates API reads every group's devices from it                                                                            |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Next steps [#next-steps]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Cards>
    <Card title="Publish and roll out an update" href="/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out" description="Create a pack, build it and roll it out to a device group." />

    <Card title="Connect a device" href="/docs/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device" description="What a device must do to receive updates in each backend." />

    <Card title="Configuration reference" href="/docs/platform/updates/reference/configuration" description="Every config field and its default." />
  </Cards>
</div>


# Connect a device (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  This guide describes the contract between a device and Lamassu Updates, for each backend. The device software is [SWUpdate](https://swupdate.org/): this page covers what the device must send and receive, not SWUpdate's own installation and configuration, which its documentation describes. Use it when a launch is running and no device moves.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Before you begin [#before-you-begin]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * A device with SWUpdate installed, and a way to run an update client: a small agent, or SWUpdate's `suricatta` module.
  * A device identity: one ID that is the same everywhere. It is the WFX client ID in native mode and the hawkBit controller ID in hawkBit mode, and it must equal the device's ID in the Lamassu device registry (see [Device management](/docs/platform/iot-fleets/device-management)).
  * The device must be a member of a Lamassu IoT device group, because a pack belongs to a group and a launch targets the group's devices. In hawkBit mode group membership is also read from the registry when `dms_endpoint` is set.
  * Native mode only: `update_domain` must be an address the device can reach. See [Configuration](/docs/platform/updates/reference/configuration). In hawkBit mode devices download from hawkBit.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Native mode: the device polls WFX [#native-mode-the-device-polls-wfx]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In native mode a launch creates one WFX job per device. The device polls WFX for jobs addressed to its ID, downloads the deliverable from the Updates API, installs it and reports each state back to WFX. Lamassu Updates reads those states from WFX to drive the launch.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Lamassu Updates
    participant W as WFX
    participant D as Device
    U->>W: create a job for the device ID
    D->>W: poll jobs addressed to its ID
    D->>U: download the .swu for its device ID
    D->>W: report INSTALLING, INSTALLED, ACTIVATED
    W-->>U: job events
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The sample device in `docker-compose.yml` (`swupdate-device1`) shows the minimum configuration. It takes three variables: `DEVICE_NAME` (its ID), `WFX_URI` (the WFX **client** API, `http://custom-wfx:8080/api/wfx/v1` inside the Compose network, `localhost:9080` from the host) and `PORT`. The WFX management API on `9081` is for the service, not for devices.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The job the device receives [#the-job-the-device-receives]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The job is addressed to the device (the WFX `clientId` is the device ID), names a workflow and is tagged with the launch (`lms://secure-updates/<launch id>`) and the group (`lms://dms/<group id>`). Its definition looks like this:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {
    "type": ["firmware"],
    "launchID": "<launch id>",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "groupID": "<group id>",
    "artifacts": [
      {
        "name": "my-firmware",
        "uri": "http://updates:10090/updates/v1/groups/<group>/distribution-sets/my-firmware/swu/download/<device-id>",
        "algorithm": "<algorithm name>",
        "iv": "<hex>"
      }
    ]
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Field                                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                            |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `type`                                                             | The pack type: `rawfile`, `firmware`, or both (`["rawfile","firmware"]`)                                                                                           |
  | `artifacts[0].uri`                                                 | Where to download the deliverable. The service appends the device ID, so each device fetches its own file. A `.swu` for SWU packs, a `.tar.gz` for `non-swu` packs |
  | `algorithm`, `iv`                                                  | Present only for an encrypted pack: the algorithm and, for shared-key packs, the hex IV or nonce. A per-device pack carries the algorithm but no `iv`              |
  | `signature_key_id`, `signature_algorithm`, `signature_certificate` | Present only for a signed pack                                                                                                                                     |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The device needs the key to decrypt, and holds it itself. For a per-device pack it is the key that SymKMS assigned to that device, and each device downloads a different file.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Downloading [#downloading]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The download answers with the bytes, or with `302` to a short-lived signed URL when presigned downloads are enabled for the build store. Make sure the device's HTTP client follows redirects. The route also answers `HEAD` and byte-range requests (`206`), so an interrupted download can resume. The URL is fixed when the pack is built, so a device never sees a new `update_domain` until you rebuild.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The states the device reports [#the-states-the-device-reports]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The device moves its job through the workflow's states, and the workflow decides who may make each move. For the `direct` workflow:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  INSTALL → INSTALLING → INSTALLED → (WFX, automatic) ACTIVATE → ACTIVATING → ACTIVATED
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The device reports `INSTALLING`, `INSTALLED`, `ACTIVATING` and `ACTIVATED`. WFX itself makes the `INSTALLED → ACTIVATE` step. From `INSTALL`, `INSTALLING`, `ACTIVATE` and `ACTIVATING` the device can move to `TERMINATED` to report a failure; `INSTALLED` has no failure transition.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Workflow                            | Used for                                                                     | Terminal states                               |
  | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
  | `wfx.workflow.dau.direct`           | SWU packs, no confirmation                                                   | `ACTIVATED` (success), `TERMINATED` (failure) |
  | `wfx.workflow.dau.phased`           | SWU packs with confirmation steps (`CREATED → DOWNLOAD → ... → ACTIVATED`)   | `ACTIVATED`, `TERMINATED`                     |
  | `wfx.workflow.dau.download-install` | `non-swu` packs: `DOWNLOAD → ... → INSTALLED`, every move made by the device | `INSTALLED`, `TERMINATED`                     |
  | `wfx.workflow.dau.simple`           | Minimal `DOWNLOAD → INSTALL → INSTALLED`                                     | `INSTALLED`, `TERMINATED`                     |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A `phased` job has moves that WFX or an operator makes, and nothing in Lamassu Updates advances them: it stays at `CREATED` until someone confirms it through WFX (the dashboard's **Next** button does that). The launch endpoints `force-version` and `sync-to-latest` use `phased` for SWU packs unless you pass a `workflow`. The workflow files are in `wfx/workflow/dau/` of the repository. The WFX HTTP API (listing jobs, updating status) is documented by [WFX](https://github.com/siemens/wfx).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit mode: the device polls hawkBit [#hawkbit-mode-the-device-polls-hawkbit]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In hawkBit mode devices do not poll Lamassu Updates. They poll hawkBit's DDI API, and Lamassu Updates reads the resulting action state from hawkBit.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Lamassu Updates
    participant H as hawkBit
    participant D as Device
    U->>H: create the rollout
    D->>H: poll the DDI API
    D->>H: download the module artifacts
    D->>H: post DDI feedback
    U->>H: read action and rollout state
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Make the device a hawkBit target [#make-the-device-a-hawkbit-target]

      The device needs a controller ID, and a target tagged `group:<id>` for its group. With `dms_endpoint` set, the service does this itself: when it reads a group's devices from the registry it creates the missing targets and tags them. Without `dms_endpoint` you create the targets and tags yourself. Either way the device must poll hawkBit with valid credentials.
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Configure SWUpdate [#configure-swupdate]

      Point the device's SWUpdate (`suricatta`) at hawkBit's URL (`hawkbit.ddi_url`, which defaults to `hawkbit.base_url`), with the tenant, the controller ID and an authentication method that your hawkBit tenant accepts. hawkBit refuses unauthenticated devices by default. With target security tokens, enable them for the tenant (`PUT /rest/v1/system/configs/authentication.targettoken.enabled` with `{"value":true}`) and give each device its target's `securityToken`, which it sends as `Authorization: TargetToken <token>`. The [hawkBit curl guide](/docs/platform/updates/guides/hawkbit-curl) shows every request.
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Point it at the right hawkBit [#point-it-at-the-right-hawkbit]

      The device must poll the **same hawkBit** that the service is configured for. A service pointed at a hawkBit with no targets builds and launches without error, and nothing downloads it. See [Troubleshooting](/docs/platform/updates/troubleshooting).
    </Step>
  </Steps>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit then hands the device every artifact of its distribution set. A pack with several modules runs several independent installs.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  When your gateway routes hawkBit's device artifact URLs (the path of `hawkbit.ddi_url`, `.../<tenant>/controller/v1/<controller>/softwaremodules/<id>/artifacts/<file>`) to Lamassu Updates, the service serves them only for modules assigned to or installed on that controller, and answers `404` otherwise. With presigned downloads on, it redirects to a signed URL of hawkBit's S3 bucket instead of streaming the file.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Signed and encrypted images [#signed-and-encrypted-images]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If the device verifies signatures, set its public key (`public-key-file` in SWUpdate's configuration) and sign the package with the matching key. If it decrypts, it needs the same key and algorithm the pack was built with. A mismatch is the usual reason an install fails silently after a successful download. [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption) explains which key, algorithm and IV each mode uses, and what the device receives.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Verify the result [#verify-the-result]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  After a launch, the device's job reaches `ACTIVATED` (or `INSTALLED` for a `non-swu` pack), the launch counters update, and the device inventory lists the pack:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  API=http://localhost:10090/updates/v1
  curl -s $API/devices/<device-id>/distribution-set-inventory
  curl -s $API/launch/<launch-id>/jobs
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  See [Publish and roll out an update](/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out#verify-the-result) for the rest of the checks.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                     | Likely cause                                                                                                                                                       |
  | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | The device never sees a job (native)                        | It polls the wrong WFX endpoint or uses a different ID than the group member. The WFX `clientId` must equal the device ID                                          |
  | The job stays at `CREATED`                                  | The launch uses `phased`. Confirm it through WFX or the dashboard, or relaunch with `direct`                                                                       |
  | The download fails with `404`                               | The pack is per-device encrypted and the device has no key, or the URL names another device. Check the pack's coverage and that the URL ends with this device's ID |
  | The download succeeds and the install fails                 | The signature or the key does not match what the device holds. See [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption)                         |
  | A `non-swu` launch looks stuck although the device finished | It was launched with `direct` or `phased`, which wait for `ACTIVATED`. Launch `non-swu` packs with `download-install`                                              |
  | The launch never advances (hawkBit)                         | The device is not polling this hawkBit, is not tagged into the group, or cannot authenticate                                                                       |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Next steps [#next-steps]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Cards>
    <Card title="Signing and encryption" href="/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption" description="Keys, algorithms and what the device must hold." />

    <Card title="hawkBit mode" href="/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode" description="How the adapter maps packs and campaigns onto hawkBit." />

    <Card title="Troubleshooting" href="/docs/platform/updates/troubleshooting" description="Updates not reaching devices, and other failures." />
  </Cards>
</div>


# Use the dashboard (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/guides/dashboard)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The Lamassu dashboard is the web interface for the Updates API. This guide follows the same update as the curl guides ([native](/docs/platform/updates/guides/native-curl) and [hawkBit](/docs/platform/updates/guides/hawkbit-curl)) through the screens. Names in bold are the labels shown in the dashboard.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The dashboard is a separate project (`lamassu-dashboard`). This guide describes it from its source and has no screenshots, so a label can differ in a newer version. The dashboard has no translations: its labels are in English.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Before you begin [#before-you-begin]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * Lamassu Updates is running and the dashboard can reach it. See [Connect it to the service](#connect-it-to-the-service).
  * A Lamassu IoT **device group** that contains the devices to update (**Device Groups** under **IoT**). A group's members are the devices that match its criteria.
  * For an SWU build with signing or encryption: a signing key in **Asymmetric Keys** or a symmetric key in **Symmetric Keys** (both under **KMS**), and, for per-device encryption, keys assigned to the devices in **Device Key Inventory** (under **IoT**).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Connect it to the service [#connect-it-to-the-service]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The dashboard talks to the Updates API at the address in `LAMASSU_UPDATES_API`, in its `public/config.js`. In the container image it comes from the environment variable of the same name.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```js
  LAMASSU_UPDATES_API: "http://localhost:10090"
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * The dashboard appends `/updates/v1` and `/symkms/v1` to it. A trailing `/updates/v1` is accepted and stripped.
  * If it is empty, the dashboard uses `LAMASSU_API`.
  * When authentication is on, every call carries the user's bearer token. The service ignores it, so put a gateway that checks it in front. See [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security).
  * It must point at the service instance that runs the backend you want to use. A service runs either native or hawkBit mode, never both: to use both at once you run two instances, each on its own port, and point the dashboard at one of them.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The dashboard reads `GET /updates/v1/capabilities` once, after you sign in, and hides what the backend cannot do. That is why the same screens look different in native and hawkBit mode. [What changes with the backend](#what-changes-with-the-backend) lists the differences. If the capabilities request fails, the dashboard assumes everything is supported and hides nothing.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To compare both backends, the user menu has an **Updates backend** switch with the options **Auto**, **native** and **hawkbit**. It appears only in development builds, or when the dashboard container runs with `DEV_OPTIONS_ENABLED=true`. Choosing native or hawkbit overrides `LAMASSU_UPDATES_API` for that browser, shows an editable **Updates API base URL** field and reloads the page. The defaults are `http://localhost:10090` (native) and `http://localhost:10091` (hawkbit) on localhost, and `<origin>/api` and `<origin>/api/hawkbit` on any other host.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Where things are [#where-things-are]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The sidebar group **OTA UPDATES MANAGER** has:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Item                  | Route                       | What it is                                                                                                                  |
  | --------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Dashboard**         | `/updates/dashboard`        | Page title **OTA Dashboard**: rollout health, campaigns requiring attention, version distribution and the upcoming schedule |
  | **OTA Devices**       | `/updates/devices`          | Every device with its installed and target version                                                                          |
  | **OTA Device Groups** | `/updates/device-groups`    | Groups, with how many devices are behind                                                                                    |
  | **Distribution Set**  | `/package-inventory`        | The update packs of every group                                                                                             |
  | **Software Modules**  | `/updates/software-modules` | The module catalog                                                                                                          |
  | **Campaigns**         | `/updates`                  | Launches: list, create, run                                                                                                 |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The group **IoT** has **Devices**, **Device Groups** (the Lamassu device registry and its groups), **Device Key Inventory** and **Platform Integrations**. The **JOB MANAGER** group (**Jobs**, **Workflows**) lists raw WFX jobs and workflows. It does not use the Updates API and does not create launches.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In the dashboard, a pack is a **distribution set** and a launch is a **campaign**.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  1. Create a distribution set [#1-create-a-distribution-set]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Open **Distribution Set**. The list shows every group's packs, with filters for device group and status, a search box and a **Refresh** button. Press **New Distribution Set**.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Field                               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | **Name**                            | At least 3 characters, no spaces. Use underscores. Native mode also accepts only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`                                                                                                 |
  | **Version**                         | Semver, default `1.0.0`                                                                                                                                                                                            |
  | **Device Group**                    | Required. A pack belongs to one group and can only be launched to its devices                                                                                                                                      |
  | **Type**                            | **Raw File** (no restart), **Firmware** (restart), **Both** or **Other Type**                                                                                                                                      |
  | **Driver**                          | Native: **SWU** builds one signed image (signing is optional), **Generic** delivers files as they are. hawkBit: **SWU** accepts only SWU modules, **Generic** accepts binaries and other files. Fixed once created |
  | **Allow previous-version download** | Lets devices download older versions of this pack                                                                                                                                                                  |
  | **Compatibility**                   | Optional launch preconditions (collapsed): devices must already carry another distribution set, or a software module, at a minimum version                                                                         |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Press **Create Distribution Set**. You land on the pack's page. The preconditions stay editable there, in **Launch Preconditions** on the **Overview** tab (**Save preconditions**).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In hawkBit mode the form has one more section, **Software modules**. A hawkBit set links built modules, so tick at least one built module there, and at most one OS module. The table lists only modules that fit the **Driver**: an SWU set hides modules delivered as raw files, and a Generic set hides modules delivered as a prebuilt SWU. If nothing fits, it says "No built module fits this driver", and you build one first (see [hawkBit: build a module first](#hawkbit-build-a-module-first)).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  On the native backend, the **Driver** also decides which workflow can install the pack: SWU packs need **Direct** or **Phased** and Generic packs need **Download-Install**. A mismatch leaves the update looking stuck after the device finishes.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  2. Add files and build (native) [#2-add-files-and-build-native]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  On the pack's page (`/updates/pack-details`) open the **Software Modules** tab. A native pack starts with one OS module named like the pack ("Not composed"). Open its row menu and choose **Add files**, drop your file, and upload it. The artifact name defaults to the file name without its extension, and the version is optional (semver). To compose the pack from more modules, use **Add module** (a new application module) or **Import module** (copy an existing one); the pack still builds one SWU.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Then press **Generate SWU** in the header. The sheet **SWU deliverable** has two tabs.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  **Build here** builds the package from the pack's artifacts:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Part                     | What to do                                                                                                                                                            |
  | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Artifacts to include** | Checkboxes, all selected by default                                                                                                                                   |
  | **sw-descriptor**        | Required. Load the file or type it in the editor. A checklist shows each file the description declares, and a file that is declared but not selected blocks the build |
  | **Signing**              | **Signing key**: none (unsigned) or a KMS key. With a key, pick a **Method** and a **Certificate**                                                                    |
  | **Encryption**, **Mode** | None, **Shared (one key for all devices)** or **Per-device (key per device)**                                                                                         |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  For shared encryption choose a **Symmetric key** and whether to encrypt the descriptor (**Encrypt the descriptor**) and all files (**Encrypt all files**), or tick individual files. For per-device encryption choose an **Algorithm** (default `Ascon-128a`). Each device then uses its own key from the device key inventory. If you choose no security the sheet says "No security selected".
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Press **Generate SWU**. The sheet uploads the sw-description, then builds. The badge becomes **Built** and the header button now reads **Regenerate SWU**. **Download SWU** appears next to it, except for a per-device pack: there is no download of the whole set, and each device's package is downloaded per device.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  **Upload pre-built** attaches a `.swu` you built elsewhere, up to the service's `max_artifact_size_mb` (10 GiB by default). It is stored and served unchanged, nothing is signed or encrypted for you, and the version becomes built and immutable.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A **non-swu** pack has **Generate Package** instead. It builds a `.tar.gz` of the selected artifacts, with optional signing and optional shared or per-device encryption (the cipher is AES-GCM), and it has an **Upload pre-built** tab too. **Download Package** fetches the result.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To change a built pack, create a new version: use **New Version** in the pack list's row menu (the dialog has **Create Version**), or **New Version to Edit** on the pack's **Artifacts** tab. The new version must be higher than the current one, and it clears the built package.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit: build a module first [#hawkbit-build-a-module-first]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In hawkBit mode a pack's files live in modules, built in the catalog.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  1. Open **Software Modules** and press **New module**. Fill in **Module name** (it cannot contain `/` or `:`), **Type** (**Application** or **OS / base image**), **Version**, the **Distribution set** (leave **Catalog only — no set** to link it later) and the **Delivery intent**:

     | Delivery intent             | Means                                                                                                                            |
     | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
     | **Build SWU from inputs**   | You provide files and a sw-description, and the service builds a `.swu`                                                          |
     | **Upload prebuilt SWU**     | You upload a finished `.swu`                                                                                                     |
     | **Deliver files unchanged** | The files are delivered as they are, and the module counts as built after a build step that can optionally encrypt and sign them |
     | **Decide later**            | Not usable yet                                                                                                                   |

  2. Add the files and, for **Build SWU from inputs**, the sw-description. The security cards offer signing and shared encryption. For **Build SWU from inputs** the switch **Build this module now** is on by default: turn it off to only store the files and build later from the row menu **Files and build**. For **Upload prebuilt SWU** there is no switch: the module is built as soon as the `.swu` is stored. For **Deliver files unchanged** the switch is **Build now**.

  3. Press **Create Module**.

  4. Create the distribution set and tick the built module.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A module linked into a set is frozen. Unlink it to change it, or add a new version from **Upgrade to a new version** in its catalog row menu. See [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The catalog also works on the native backend: it lists the modules of every pack, and **New module** can leave a module in **Catalog only — no set** until you add it to a pack with **Import module**. Native import copies the module, while hawkBit linking shares it.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  3. Start a campaign [#3-start-a-campaign]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Press **Start Campaign** in the pack's row menu in **Distribution Set** (enabled once the pack is built), or **New Campaign** on the **Campaigns** page. The form, **Create campaign**, is at `/updates/new`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Section                | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
  | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Campaign basics**    | **Campaign name (optional)**, **Distribution set**. **Device group** and **Driver** are inherited and read-only. **Workflow**: on native, every registered WFX workflow (Direct, Phased, Download-Install...), with a warning when it does not fit the driver. On hawkBit the field is **Install mode**: **Forced** (the device installs as soon as it polls) or **Soft** (the device may confirm or postpone) |
  | **Schedule**           | **Start as soon as it is executed** or **Start at a planned time** (date and time, in your browser's time zone)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
  | **Batching & rollout** | **Batch mode** (**Fixed count** or **Percentage**), the batch size or percentage, and the switch **Auto rollout**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | **Safety controls**    | Only with Auto rollout on: **Approval threshold** (%) and **Error threshold** (%)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | **Optional**           | **Test device** (the canary, updated first), the set's **Preconditions** (read-only), **Notes**, **Weight**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  There is no device picker. A campaign targets every device of the pack's group, and the **Campaign summary** panel shows how many match and the estimated number of batches.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If the pack has preconditions, the dashboard first runs a dry run and shows **Campaign preconditions**: how many devices qualify, who does not and why. Tick **Force deploy to non-qualifying devices (not recommended)** to send to them anyway, then **Confirm campaign**.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Press **Create campaign**. The campaign is created but nothing is sent yet: you return to **Campaigns**.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  4. Run and watch the campaign [#4-run-and-watch-the-campaign]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  On **Campaigns** (`/updates`) each row has the progress, the status (such as **Scheduled**, **Rolling Out**, **Paused**, **Completed**, **Cancelled**) and the batch progress. The tiles at the top (**Active campaigns**, **Scheduled**, **Rolling out**, **Requires attention**, **Completed**) filter the list. The page refreshes every four seconds while anything is moving.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The row's main button releases a batch:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * **Send to test device** sends the canary first.
  * **Execute next batch** sends the next batch.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  It is hidden when the campaign is completed or cancelled, paused, scheduled for later, has nothing pending, or is an **Auto rollout** campaign that is already running. While the canary is being tested or has failed, it stays visible but disabled. A failed canary pauses a native campaign: use **Resume** to retry it. A scheduled campaign starts by itself at its planned time.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The row menu has **Open details**, **Resume**, **Pause**, **Retry N failed** and **Cancel campaign** (it asks "Cancel Campaign?"). **Pause** stops further batches while devices already in flight finish; **Resume** continues. There is no button for marking a campaign complete: a native campaign completes by itself when no device is pending or in progress.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Below the table, a panel shows the selected campaign's **Batches** and a **Device progress** table. It follows the first active row until you select another. Open **View** for `/updates/details`:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * **Overview**: identity, preconditions, and the **Rollout Configuration** (workflow or install mode, rollout type and value, auto mode, test device). **Edit** on the rollout value works only where the backend supports editing a running strategy.
  * **Device Jobs**: one row per device with its job state, a **Refresh Jobs** button and, per row, a **Workflow** button that opens the device's timeline. For the Phased workflow, a **Next** button and a strip of transitions let you confirm steps, which is how a `phased` campaign moves on.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The page header repeats the main button (**Execute Campaign**, or **Send to Test Device** before the canary) and **Retry N failed device(s)**. It has no pause, resume or cancel: those are in the list's row menu. On hawkBit, **Pause** is hidden until the campaign has started dispatching.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  5. Follow devices [#5-follow-devices]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Open **Devices** (under **IoT**) and pick a device. The page has more tabs than the update-related ones listed here:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Tab                   | Shows                                                                                                     |
  | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Information**       | The distribution sets it carries, and **Up to date** or **Outdated** against the declared target          |
  | **Update Status**     | Native: the WFX event workflow. hawkBit: the current update with Assigned, Installing and Installed steps |
  | **Package Inventory** | **Installed Distribution Sets** with their artifacts, and the **Pack Update History**                     |
  | **Jobs**              | The device's WFX jobs                                                                                     |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Use **Launch Update...** in the device's actions menu to send one version to one device. The dialog **Launch update for device** asks for the device group (when the device is in several), the distribution set, the version and the workflow (or install mode), and creates one job. The pack's own actions menu has **Targeted Update**, which does the same for devices you tick in a list, always with the `direct` workflow, and it is enabled once the pack is built. On **OTA Devices**, select devices of one group and press **Update** to do it for many devices; the button is disabled when the selection spans several groups.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  **OTA Dashboard**, **OTA Devices** and **OTA Device Groups** show version compliance: which devices are up to date, behind a declared target, or have no target. A group's page also lists the version each device runs against the group's released version, with an **Update to vX** button for the outdated ones. Without version-compliance support on the backend they still list devices and campaigns, but target versions show as **No target** or an em dash, with the alert "Target versions unavailable on this backend".
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  What changes with the backend [#what-changes-with-the-backend]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Screen                 | Native                                                                                                                                                      | hawkBit                                                                                                                                                                                 |
  | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Pack list              | Status, packaging and **Built / Not built / Build failed** tiles                                                                                            | Those tiles, the status filter and column are hidden. A set has no build state of its own: it is ready when all its modules are built, and **Start Campaign** stays disabled until then |
  | New pack               | No modules section                                                                                                                                          | Required **Software modules** section                                                                                                                                                   |
  | Pack page header       | **Generate SWU** and **Download SWU** (or **Generate Package** and **Download Package**)                                                                    | A **Software modules** button instead: build in the catalog                                                                                                                             |
  | Pack page tabs         | **Overview**, **Software Modules**, **Contents**, **Manifest**, **Version History** (composition is supported, so there is no pack-level **Artifacts** tab) | The same. The **Artifacts** tab appears instead only if the hawkBit server lacks the module types                                                                                       |
  | Security               | On the **Generate SWU** sheet                                                                                                                               | Per module                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | Campaign form          | **Workflow**: Direct, Phased or any registered WFX workflow                                                                                                 | **Install mode**: **Forced** or **Soft**                                                                                                                                                |
  | Error threshold        | The campaign is cancelled once this % of all its devices have failed                                                                                        | The campaign stops when more than this % of a batch fails                                                                                                                               |
  | **Update Status** tab  | WFX event workflow                                                                                                                                          | hawkBit action steps                                                                                                                                                                    |
  | Edit a running rollout | Supported                                                                                                                                                   | Not supported                                                                                                                                                                           |
  | Module catalog         | Modules are created without a set or added to a pack, and import copies them                                                                                | Modules are built in the catalog, and a pack links them                                                                                                                                 |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The **Manifest** tab (the signed version manifest) appears only when the backend supports artifact signatures.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Not in the dashboard [#not-in-the-dashboard]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  These API features have no screen: marking a campaign complete (`/complete`), syncing all of a device's sets to the group's latest versions at once (`/sync-to-latest`), and declaring a group's latest version. Use the [API](/docs/platform/updates/reference/api) for them. To push one set to one device, **Launch Update...** and the per-device **Update to vX** button on a group's page do it.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                          | Likely cause                                                                                                                                                                |
  | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Screens or buttons that should exist are missing                 | The capabilities request succeeded and the backend does not support them. Check **Updates backend** in the user menu (development builds) or `GET /updates/v1/capabilities` |
  | Update screens fail to load or show errors                       | `LAMASSU_UPDATES_API` points at the wrong service or port, or your gateway does not route `/updates/v1`                                                                     |
  | **Start Campaign** is disabled                                   | The pack is not built (native), or not every module is built (hawkBit)                                                                                                      |
  | No device group is offered when creating a pack                  | No device group exists yet. Create one under **Device Groups**                                                                                                              |
  | A campaign looks stuck in **Rolling Out** after devices finished | The workflow does not match the pack's driver. SWU packs need **Direct** or **Phased**; Generic packs need **Download-Install**                                             |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Next steps [#next-steps]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Cards>
    <Card title="Publish and roll out an update" href="/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out" description="The same flow as API requests." />

    <Card title="Concepts" href="/docs/platform/updates/concepts" description="Packs, modules, campaigns and workflows." />

    <Card title="Capabilities" href="/docs/platform/updates/reference/capabilities" description="What each backend supports and what the UI hides." />
  </Cards>
</div>


# Update flow with curl, hawkBit backend (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/guides/hawkbit-curl)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The same update as in the [native guide](/docs/platform/updates/guides/native-curl), against the service in hawkBit mode. The management requests go to Lamassu Updates. The device side is a different protocol: devices poll hawkBit's DDI API, not this service and not WFX. The commands were run against a real hawkBit 1.1.0, and the responses are real, trimmed where long. Examples that say they were not run were checked against the code only.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The differences from native mode, in short:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  |                            | Native                                                                 | hawkBit                                                               |
  | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Build                      | Upload artifacts and a sw-description to the pack, then build the pack | Build a **module** in the catalog first, then create the pack from it |
  | Pack after creation        | `draft`                                                                | Already `built`                                                       |
  | Who tells the device       | WFX job                                                                | hawkBit action, read over DDI                                         |
  | Device reports to          | WFX                                                                    | hawkBit (DDI feedback)                                                |
  | Next batch, with `auto` on | The service, from WFX events                                           | hawkBit, from its rollout groups                                      |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Before you begin [#before-you-begin]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * The [stack is running](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode) in hawkBit mode: this service, its Postgres, hawkBit and the Lamassu device manager.
  * A device group in Lamassu with devices in it. This guide uses `fleet-a` with `dev-001` to `dev-004`.
  * `curl` and `jq`.
  * A SWU builder configured (`swugenerator_path`), to build a `swu-build` module. Without one, `POST .../build` on such a module answers `501`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  API=http://localhost:10090/updates/v1
  HB=http://localhost:8090                                  # hawkBit
  HB_AUTH="admin:${HAWKBIT_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}"          # hawkBit Management API login
  GROUP=fleet-a
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Callout type="info" title="Ports and gateways">
    `config-hawkbit.yml` in the repository serves the API on port `10090`, like the native stack, so run one backend at a time on that port. `config-hawkbit-demo.yml` serves it on `10091`, which the repository's dashboard development setup points at for the hawkBit backend. Set `API` to wherever your instance listens. Through a Lamassu gateway the API is usually `https://lamassu.example.com/api/updates/v1` and each call needs your gateway credential, for example `-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`.
  </Callout>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  1. Check the backend [#1-check-the-backend]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s $API/capabilities | jq -c '{backend, unsupported}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"backend":"hawkbit","unsupported":["per_device_encryption","workflows","launch_strategy_update","launch_complete","launch_device_assignment","push_events","prebuilt_deliverable"]}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `artifact_encryption`, `software_module_composition`, `standalone_software_modules` and `software_module_replace` appear in that list too if the build settings or hawkBit's module types are missing. See [Capabilities](/docs/platform/updates/reference/capabilities).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  2. Create a module in the catalog [#2-create-a-module-in-the-catalog]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A hawkBit distribution set can only link **built** modules, so the module comes first. `delivery_intent` says how it ships: `swu-build` builds a `.swu` from your files and a sw-description. See [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode) for the other intents (`swu-prebuilt`, `raw`).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  MID=$(curl -s -X POST $API/softwaremodules -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"type":"os","name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","delivery_intent":"swu-build"}' | jq -r .id)
  curl -s $API/softwaremodules/by-id/$MID | jq -c '{id,key,built,delivery_intent}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"id":"1","key":"os:water-panel","built":false,"delivery_intent":"swu-build"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `type` is `os` or `application`, and `type`, `name` and `version` are required. Without a `delivery_intent` the module is `undecided`, which accepts files but cannot be built or linked until you choose one with `PUT /softwaremodules/by-id/$MID`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  3. Upload the file and the sw-description [#3-upload-the-file-and-the-sw-description]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Use the same `index.html` and `sw-description` as in the [native guide](/docs/platform/updates/guides/native-curl).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/softwaremodules/by-id/$MID/artifacts -F file=@index.html
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"id":"hb:1:1","name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","filename":"index.html","checksum":"c400a4f1...","size":52}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/softwaremodules/by-id/$MID/descriptor -F file=@sw-description | jq -c '{id,built,artifacts: [.artifacts[].filename]}'
  # {"id":"1","built":false,"artifacts":["index.html"]}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A `swu-build` module refuses a finished `.swu` as input, and a `swu-prebuilt` module takes exactly one `.swu`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  4. Build the module [#4-build-the-module]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/softwaremodules/by-id/$MID/build -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
  # {"msg":"Software module built"}

  curl -s $API/softwaremodules/by-id/$MID | jq -c '{built, locked, files: [.artifacts[] | {filename,size}]}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"built":true,"locked":false,"files":[{"filename":"water-panel.swu","size":1024}]}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Building replaced the module's input files with the finished `.swu`. The build body is optional. To encrypt or sign, send `user`, `encryption_key_name`, `encryption_alg_name`, `signature_key_id`, `signature_alg_name` and `signature_certificate`, as in the [signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption) page. A module can be built once: to change it, release a new version of the module.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  5. Create the pack from the built module [#5-create-the-pack-from-the-built-module]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"name\":\"water-panel\",\"version\":\"1.0.0\",\"group_id\":\"fleet-a\",\"type\":\"rawfile\",\"packaging\":\"swu\",\"modules\":[{\"source_module_id\":\"$MID\"}]}" \
    | jq -c '{id,name,version,status}'
  # {"id":"1","name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","status":"built"}

  curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets | jq -r '.list[0].uri'
  # http://localhost:8090/DEFAULT/controller/v1/{controllerId}/softwaremodules/1/artifacts/water-panel.swu
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The pack is built from the start. Its `uri` is a hawkBit download address that devices resolve themselves. In hawkBit mode `modules` takes only `source_module_id` entries, and each module must be built and compatible with the pack's packaging. Several entries make a multi-module pack, and then `GET .../swu/download` answers `400`: download each module's deliverable with `GET .../modules/:moduleKey/artifact/download`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  6. Preview the launch, then create it [#6-preview-the-launch-then-create-it]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A group's devices only exist in hawkBit once the service has registered them. The service does that whenever it lists the group's devices, which a launch, a dry run, a job listing or a compliance read all do. The canary check runs **before** that, so on the first launch of a group that has not been listed yet, a `test_device_id` fails:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
