  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST "$API/groups/$GROUP/launch?dry_run=true" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2,"test_device_id":"dev-001"}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"err":"Failed to create launch history: test device dev-001 cannot act as this group's canary: device dev-001 does not exist"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Run the dry run without a canary first. It registers the group's devices in hawkBit as targets and tags them `group:fleet-a`:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST "$API/groups/$GROUP/launch?dry_run=true" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2}' | jq -c .
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"never_seen_devices":["dev-001","dev-002","dev-003","dev-004"],"precondition_failures":[],"qualifying_devices":["dev-001","dev-002","dev-003","dev-004"],"superseded_devices":null}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `never_seen_devices` lists targets that have not contacted hawkBit yet. A rollout group cannot finish while its devices never poll, so check this list. `superseded_devices` lists devices that already have an update in flight: creating the launch **cancels** those actions, because hawkBit replaces a target's unfinished actions with the new one. Now create the launch with the canary:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  LAUNCH=$(curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2,"test_device_id":"dev-001","name":"water-panel 1.0.0 wave 1"}' \
    | jq -r .launch_id)
  echo $LAUNCH     # 1: the id of the hawkBit rollout
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `workflow_type` has no WFX meaning here: `phased` makes a hawkBit `soft` action (the device decides when to install) and anything else a `forced` one. Define a helper to follow the launch:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  status() {
    curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/launch | jq -c --arg id "$LAUNCH" \
      '.list[] | select(.id==$id) | {status,pending_count,active_count,completed_count,failed_count}'
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To start the rollout later, add `scheduled_at` (RFC 3339) to the create body. hawkBit's own scheduler then starts it, and a `rollout` call before that time leaves the schedule alone. Not run here.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  7. Start the rollout [#7-start-the-rollout]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/rollout
  # {"message":"Launch history executed successfully"}
  status
  # {"status":"running","pending_count":3,"active_count":1,"completed_count":0,"failed_count":0}

  curl -s -u "$HB_AUTH" $HB/rest/v1/rollouts | jq -c '.content[] | {id,name,status,totalTargets,type}'
  # {"id":1,"name":"water-panel 1.0.0 wave 1","status":"running","totalTargets":4,"type":"forced"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The service started a hawkBit rollout: the canary in the first group and the rest after it.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  8. Play the device (DDI) [#8-play-the-device-ddi]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A real device runs SWUpdate's `suricatta`, which does this itself. These are the requests it makes.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  First, devices must authenticate. hawkBit's default is to refuse them. Enable security tokens for the tenant once, and read the target's token:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -u "$HB_AUTH" -X PUT $HB/rest/v1/system/configs/authentication.targettoken.enabled \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"value":true}'
  TOKEN=$(curl -s -u "$HB_AUTH" $HB/rest/v1/targets/dev-001 | jq -r .securityToken)
  AUTH="Authorization: TargetToken $TOKEN"
  DDI=$HB/DEFAULT/controller/v1
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  This is the local setup. In a deployment where devices reach hawkBit through the Lamassu gateway, `hawkbit.ddi_url` is the gateway path (for example `https://lamassu.example.com/api/hawkbit-ddi`) and devices authenticate as the gateway requires, typically with their client certificate. See [Connect a device](/docs/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Poll. When there is work, the answer links to a `deploymentBase`:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -H "$AUTH" $DDI/dev-001 | jq
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {
    "config": {"polling": {"sleep": "00:05:00"}},
    "_links": {
      "deploymentBase": {"href": "http://localhost:8090/DEFAULT/controller/v1/dev-001/deploymentBase/1?c=411629670"},
      "configData": {"href": "http://localhost:8090/DEFAULT/controller/v1/dev-001/configData"}
    }
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Read the deployment and download its artifact:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  DEP=$(curl -s -H "$AUTH" $DDI/dev-001 | jq -r '._links.deploymentBase.href')
  curl -s -H "$AUTH" "$DEP" | jq -c '{action: .id, download: .deployment.download, update: .deployment.update,
    chunks: [.deployment.chunks[] | {part,name,version, artifacts: [.artifacts[] | {filename,size}]}]}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"action":"1","download":"forced","update":"forced","chunks":[{"part":"os","name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","artifacts":[{"filename":"water-panel.swu","size":1024}]}]}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  ACTION=$(curl -s -H "$AUTH" "$DEP" | jq -r .id)
  curl -s -H "$AUTH" -o water.swu -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} bytes\n' \
    $DDI/dev-001/softwaremodules/1/artifacts/water-panel.swu
  # 200 1024 bytes
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  When the service publishes the device artifact URL (the `ddi_url` path), it serves that same route itself, for modules in the device's assigned or installed set only, and with S3 presigning enabled it answers `302` to a short-lived signed URL. A device does not need to know the difference: it follows the redirect.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Report progress and the result. `closed` with `finished: success` is the end:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -H "$AUTH" -X POST $DDI/dev-001/deploymentBase/$ACTION/feedback -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"status":{"execution":"proceeding","result":{"finished":"none"},"details":["installing"]}}'
  curl -s -H "$AUTH" -X POST $DDI/dev-001/deploymentBase/$ACTION/feedback -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"status":{"execution":"closed","result":{"finished":"success"},"details":["installed"]}}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The service reads hawkBit when you ask, so the launch is up to date:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  status
  # {"status":"running","pending_count":3,"active_count":0,"completed_count":1,"failed_count":0}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To report a failure, send `"finished":"failure"` in the `closed` feedback.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  9. Release the next batches [#9-release-the-next-batches]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  With `auto` off, hawkBit pauses after each group. Each `rollout` call releases the next one:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/rollout
  curl -s $API/launch/$LAUNCH/jobs | jq -r '.list[] | "\(.clientId) \(.status.state)"'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  dev-001 ACTIVATED
  dev-002 DOWNLOADING
  dev-003 DOWNLOADING
  dev-004 CREATED
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Here a hawkBit action is shown as a workflow state: a scheduled action is `CREATED`, a running one `DOWNLOADING` (hawkBit does not report finer steps), a finished one (or one that finished with a warning) `ACTIVATED`, and a failed, cancelled or cancelling one `TERMINATED`. Repeat step 8 for `dev-002` and `dev-003` (the token comes from each target), then call `rollout` once more for `dev-004`. When every action is finished:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"status":"completed","pending_count":0,"active_count":0,"completed_count":4,"failed_count":0}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit decides when a batch is finished. After the last device of a batch reports, hawkBit pauses the rollout, and for a moment its group still reads `running`. The service cannot tell that pause from one an operator made, so a `rollout` call in that window answers `400` with `rollout 1 is paused; resume it first`. Call `resume` and hawkBit releases the next batch itself:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/resume
  # {"message":"Launch resumed","status":"running"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  10. Check the result [#10-check-the-result]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s $API/devices/dev-001/distribution-set-inventory | jq -c '.list[] | {distribution_set_name,version,installed_at,artifacts: [.artifacts[].artifact_name]}'
  # {"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","installed_at":"2026-10-21T07:39:23.345+02:00","artifacts":["water-panel.swu"]}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Things that behave differently [#things-that-behave-differently]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * **Automatic rollout.** With `auto: true`, hawkBit advances the groups itself once `approval_threshold` is met. The service does not run an event consumer in this mode. The thresholds are set on every rollout group, and hawkBit evaluates both percentages **per group**, not against all devices as native does. An unset or `0` threshold becomes 100, so an unset `error_threshold` never trips. The canary group always needs 100%. They apply with `auto` off too.
  * **A tripped error threshold.** hawkBit then pauses the rollout, and the service reports the launch as `cancelled`. `resume` and `rollout` both answer `400` for it.
  * **Pause and resume.** `pause` and `resume` map to hawkBit's rollout pause and resume, but only a pause an operator made can be resumed. hawkBit already holds the rollout between groups when `auto` is off, so `pause` then answers `400` ("Rollout can only be paused in state running but current state is paused") and `resume` answers `400` ("not paused; use Execute to release the next batch"). Use `rollout` to release the next group.
  * **Strategy read-back.** The strategy shown for a launch is derived from the hawkBit rollout's groups, not stored. A launch created with a fixed batch of 2 for 4 devices reads back as `percentage` 50.
  * **Static membership.** A rollout is built from the devices of the group when the launch is created. Devices added to the group later are not picked up (`launch_device_assignment` is unsupported).
  * **Not available.** Per-device encryption, custom workflows (`GET /workflows` returns an empty list), editing a running strategy, marking a launch complete, pushed job events (progress is polled), set-level prebuilt upload, and building a pack directly. `POST .../swu` answers `501`:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  {"err":"Failed to execute update pack: operation not supported by the active updates backend: hawkbit mode: a distribution set is not built directly — build each software module in the Software Modules catalog, then link the built modules into the ..."}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                                               | Cause and fix                                                                                                             |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `501` building a module: no SWU builder                                               | `swugenerator_path` is not configured. Configure it, or upload a prebuilt `.swu` with intent `swu-prebuilt`               |
  | `501` building a module: no SymKMS or no KMS endpoint                                 | Encryption needs `symkms_endpoint` and signing needs `kms_endpoint`. Build without those fields, or configure them        |
  | `400 ... is not built` creating a pack                                                | A module linked into a pack must be built first. Build it in the catalog                                                  |
  | `400 ... incompatible with distribution set packaging`                                | A `raw` module cannot go into a `swu` pack, and a `swu-prebuilt` module cannot go into a `non-swu` pack                   |
  | `400 ... frozen` changing a module                                                    | A module linked to a pack is frozen. Edit and build it in the catalog, then link it again                                 |
  | `400 ... already built`                                                               | A module is built once. Release a new version of the module                                                               |
  | `409 ... being built or changed by another request`                                   | Another request holds the module. Retry when it finishes                                                                  |
  | Creating a module answers `400` mentioning that hawkBit reserves the name and version | hawkBit keeps the name and version of a module that was assigned to a device, even after it is deleted. Use a new version |
  | The canary fails with `device ... does not exist`                                     | The group's devices are not in hawkBit yet. Run a dry run without `test_device_id` first                                  |
  | A launch never advances                                                               | Check `never_seen_devices`: a device that never polls blocks its rollout group                                            |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Next steps [#next-steps]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode) for modules, delivery intents and what lives where
  * [Connect a device](/docs/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device) for the device-side setup
  * [API reference](/docs/platform/updates/reference/api)
  * [Troubleshooting](/docs/platform/updates/troubleshooting)
</div>


# Update flow with curl, native backend (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/guides/native-curl)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A complete update, request by request: create a pack, build it, send it to a group in batches, play the device, and follow progress. Every command was run against a native-mode stack, and the responses are real, trimmed where long, except where a section says it was not run: those examples were checked against the code only.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If you use the [hawkBit backend](/docs/platform/updates/guides/hawkbit-curl) the flow differs, mainly in how a pack is built and how devices report. For the screens that do the same, see the [dashboard guide](/docs/platform/updates/guides/dashboard).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Before you begin [#before-you-begin]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * The [stack is running](/docs/platform/updates/getting-started) in native mode: the service, Postgres, WFX and the Lamassu device manager.
  * A device group exists in Lamassu with devices in it. This guide uses the group `fleet-a` with the devices `dev-001` to `dev-004`.
  * `curl` and `jq` are installed. `jq` is only used to pull values out of responses.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  API=http://localhost:10090/updates/v1
  WFX=http://localhost:9080/api/wfx/v1      # WFX client API: what a device talks to
  GROUP=fleet-a
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  These are the addresses of the Docker Compose stack in the repository. Through a Lamassu gateway the API is usually `https://lamassu.example.com/api/updates/v1`, and every call then needs the credential your gateway requires, for example `-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`. The service itself does no authentication. See [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  1. Check the backend [#1-check-the-backend]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s $API/capabilities | jq -c '{backend, unsupported}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"backend":"native","unsupported":["software_module_deliverables","software_module_replace"]}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  2. Create the pack [#2-create-the-pack]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","group_id":"fleet-a","type":"rawfile","packaging":"swu"}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"id":"bb74c7e1-ae3d-450b-bc73-6ed2d761934f","name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","group_id":"fleet-a",
   "type":"rawfile","packaging":"swu","status":"draft","uri":"", ...}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The pack is `draft`. It stays editable until it is built. `name`, `version` (semver) and `group_id` are required; the name must be unique in the group, or the request answers `409`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  3. Upload the sw-description and the artifact [#3-upload-the-sw-description-and-the-artifact]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The sw-description tells SWUpdate what to install. This minimal one installs a web page. See the sw-description rules in [Publish and roll out an update](/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  cat > sw-description <<'EOD'
  software =
  {
  	version = "1.0.0";
  	description = "Water panel";
  	hardware-compatibility: [ "1.0" ];
  	images: (
  		{
  			filename = "index.html";
  			path = "/web/index.html";
  			type = "rawfile";
  			compressed = "zlib";
  			properties: {
  				decompressed-size = "52";
  			};
  		}
  	);
  }
  EOD
  printf '<html><body><h1>Water panel v1.0</h1></body></html>\n' > index.html

  P=$API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/water-panel

  curl -s -X POST $P/descriptor/upload -F file=@sw-description
  # {"msg":"Descriptor uploaded successfully"}

  ART=$(curl -s -X POST $P/artifact/upload \
    -F file=@index.html -F artifact_name=index.html -F version=1.0.0 | jq -r .artifact.id)
  echo $ART
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  31e034d1-9dfa-43d9-ac6b-45fa79e2d51d
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The artifact name is global: all packs share one catalog, and a name can only be reused with a **higher** `version`. Uploading `index.html` again as `1.0.0` fails with `version 1.0.0 must be greater than the current latest version`. A file named `.swu` or `.tar.gz` must really be one, or the upload answers `400`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  4. Build the .swu [#4-build-the-swu]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `selected_artifact_ids` is what puts artifacts into the build. Without it the build fails.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $P/swu -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"selected_artifact_ids\":[\"$ART\"]}"
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"message":"Update pack executed successfully"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets | jq -c '.list[] | {name,version,status,uri}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","status":"built","uri":"http://updates:10090/updates/v1/groups/fleet-a/distribution-sets/water-panel/swu/download"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `uri` starts with the service's `update_domain`. In the Compose stack that is `http://updates:10090/updates/v1/` (`config-docker.yml`), a name that resolves only inside the Compose network, because it is the address devices use. From your host, call the same path on `localhost:10090`, as the next command does.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The pack is now `built`: artifacts can no longer be added or linked to it. You can fetch the shared package (this one is not encrypted):
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -o water.swu -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} bytes\n' $P/swu/download
  # 200 1024 bytes
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Downloads support `Range` and `HEAD`, so a client can learn the size first and resume an interrupted transfer, for example with `curl -C - -o water.swu $P/swu/download`. With S3 storage and presigning enabled, the same request can answer `302` to a short-lived signed URL, which `curl -L` follows.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If the build fails, the pack gets the status `build_failed` and `last_build_error` holds the reason. It stays editable: fix the cause and build again.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  5. Preview, then create the launch [#5-preview-then-create-the-launch]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A dry run shows who would receive the update, without creating anything:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST "$API/groups/$GROUP/launch?dry_run=true" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2,"test_device_id":"dev-001"}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"never_seen_devices":null,"precondition_failures":[],
   "qualifying_devices":["dev-001","dev-002","dev-003","dev-004"],"superseded_devices":null}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Create it. `test_device_id` is the canary: it goes alone first and must succeed before anyone else is touched. `rollout_value` 2 means batches of two devices.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  LAUNCH=$(curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2,"test_device_id":"dev-001","name":"water-panel 1.0.0 wave 1"}' \
    | jq -r .launch_id)
  echo $LAUNCH
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  98af8db7-b3a0-4802-8cde-269d88e6723e
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A small helper makes the launch easy to follow in the next steps:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  status() {
    curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/launch | jq -c --arg id "$LAUNCH" \
      '.list[] | select(.id==$id) | {status,pending_count,active_count,completed_count,failed_count,test_device_status}'
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  6. Roll out the canary [#6-roll-out-the-canary]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/rollout
  # {"message":"Launch history executed successfully"}

  status
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"status":"","pending_count":3,"active_count":1,"completed_count":0,"failed_count":0,"test_device_status":"active"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  An empty `status` means running. Only the canary is active. The service created one WFX job for `dev-001`:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s $API/launch/$LAUNCH/jobs | jq -r '.list[] | "\(.clientId) \(.status.state)"'
  # dev-001 INSTALL
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  7. Play the device [#7-play-the-device]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A real device does this by itself. These commands are what it sends to WFX, so you can drive a test device by hand. First the device asks WFX for its job:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s "$WFX/jobs?clientId=dev-001&state=INSTALL" | jq '.content[0] | {id, state: .status.state, definition}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {
    "id": "35bf5512-1aa3-46e6-9a72-2096560e8bf0",
    "state": "INSTALL",
    "definition": {
      "artifacts": [
        {"name": "water-panel",
         "uri": "http://updates:10090/updates/v1/groups/fleet-a/distribution-sets/water-panel/swu/download/dev-001"}
      ],
      "groupID": "fleet-a",
      "launchID": "98af8db7-b3a0-4802-8cde-269d88e6723e",
      "type": ["rawfile"],
      "version": "1.0.0"
    }
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The device downloads the `uri`, installs it, and reports each step:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  JOB=$(curl -s "$WFX/jobs?clientId=dev-001&state=INSTALL" | jq -r '.content[0].id')
  # A device resolves "updates" itself; from the host, swap in localhost
  curl -s -o water-dev-001.swu "$(curl -s $WFX/jobs/$JOB | jq -r '.definition.artifacts[0].uri' | sed 's#//updates:#//localhost:#')"

  for state in INSTALLING INSTALLED; do
    curl -s -X PUT $WFX/jobs/$JOB/status -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"state\":\"$state\"}"
  done
  curl -s $WFX/jobs/$JOB | jq -r .status.state      # ACTIVATE: WFX moved it on by itself

  for state in ACTIVATING ACTIVATED; do
    curl -s -X PUT $WFX/jobs/$JOB/status -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"state\":\"$state\"}"
  done
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `direct` workflow is `INSTALL → INSTALLING → INSTALLED → ACTIVATE → ACTIVATING → ACTIVATED`. WFX itself makes the `INSTALLED → ACTIVATE` step. To report a failure, move a job to `TERMINATED`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The service hears about every change from WFX through its event stream and updates the launch. This takes a moment, so if `status` still shows the device as active, run it again after a second:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  sleep 2; status
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"status":"","pending_count":3,"active_count":0,"completed_count":1,"failed_count":0,"test_device_status":"completed"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  8. Roll out the rest [#8-roll-out-the-rest]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The canary passed. Each `rollout` call now sends the next batch of two:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/rollout
  curl -s $API/launch/$LAUNCH/jobs | jq -r '.list[] | select(.status.state=="INSTALL") | .clientId'
  # dev-003
  # dev-004
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Walk those devices through steps like in step 7, then call `rollout` again for the last device. When nothing is pending or active the launch completes by itself:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"status":"completed","pending_count":0,"active_count":0,"completed_count":4,"failed_count":0}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `completed_count` counts only successes: a failed device is counted in `failed_count`. A launch is marked `completed` once nothing is pending or active, even if some devices failed, so check `failed_count` before you call the update a success.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  9. Check the result [#9-check-the-result]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  # What a device carries now, with its artifacts
  curl -s $API/devices/dev-001/distribution-set-inventory | jq -c '.list[] | {distribution_set_name,version,installed_at}'
  # {"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","version":"1.0.0","installed_at":"2026-10-21T07:35:49.434581+02:00"}

  # The history of update attempts
  curl -s $API/devices/dev-001/distribution-set-updates | jq -c '.list[] | {version_from,version_to,status}'
  # {"version_from":"","version_to":"1.0.0","status":"success"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To track drift, declare the version devices should be on, then read compliance:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  PACK=$(curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets | jq -r '.list[] | select(.name=="water-panel") | .id')
  curl -s -X PUT $API/groups/$GROUP/latest-distribution-sets/$PACK \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"1.0.0"}'
  curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/version-status | jq -c '.rows[] | {device_id,current_version,latest_version,in_sync}'
  curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/version-compliance
  # {"group_id":"fleet-a","devices":[]}      no device is out of date
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The fleet-wide view of the last attempt per device and pack, including attempts outside any launch, is one call. Not run here; the brackets of a filter need `curl -g`:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -sg "$API/devices/distribution-set-updates/latest?filter=status[eq]failed" | jq -c '.list[] | {device_id,distribution_set_name,version_to,status}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Variations [#variations]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Let the service release the batches [#let-the-service-release-the-batches]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  With `auto` on, the service sends the next batch itself once enough of the current one succeeded. `approval_threshold` is the percentage of the batch that must succeed (0 or 100 mean all of it). `error_threshold` applies to every launch, `auto` or not: the launch is cancelled once the number of failed devices reaches that percentage of **all** devices, rounded up. With 4 devices at 75%, the third failure cancels it.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  This example uses a second pack, `valve-panel`, created and built like `water-panel` (steps 2 to 4). Artifact names are global and a name that already exists must get a higher version, so give this one its own file name:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  PV=$API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/valve-panel
  curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name":"valve-panel","version":"1.0.0","group_id":"'$GROUP'","type":"rawfile","packaging":"swu"}'
  cp index.html valve.html
  sed 's/index.html/valve.html/' sw-description > sw-valve
  curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST $PV/descriptor/upload -F file=@sw-valve
  AV=$(curl -s -X POST $PV/artifact/upload -F file=@valve.html -F artifact_name=valve.html -F version=1.0.0 | jq -r .artifact.id)
  curl -s -X POST $PV/swu -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"selected_artifact_ids\":[\"$AV\"]}"

  LAUNCH=$(curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"valve-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2,
         "auto":true,"approval_threshold":50,"error_threshold":75,"name":"valve auto"}' | jq -r .launch_id)
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Call `rollout` once to start. A second call is refused:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/rollout
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  {"err":"Failed to execute launch history: operation not valid in the current state: launch 72afe5f7-... rolls out automatically: its next batch is released once the current one meets the approval threshold"}   [400]
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If one device of the first batch fails (`TERMINATED`) and the other succeeds, 50% succeeded meets the threshold and the next batch is dispatched on its own.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Pause, resume, retry and cancel [#pause-resume-retry-and-cancel]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/pause     # {"message":"Launch paused","status":"paused"}
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/resume    # {"message":"Launch resumed","status":"running"}
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/retry-failed
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/cancel    # {"message":"Launch cancelled","status":"cancelled"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A pause lets the batch in flight finish and holds the next one. `retry-failed` puts the failed devices back in the pending pool and releases the next batch. That batch is drawn at random from all pending devices, so it can also contain devices that were never sent, and if more devices failed than fit in a batch only one batch goes out. It answers `400` when nothing failed, and it re-opens a completed or cancelled launch (`"status":"running"`). A failed canary pauses the launch by itself, and `resume` then sends the canary again. A cancelled launch cannot be resumed, and in-flight devices finish their current job.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Schedule a launch [#schedule-a-launch]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Not run here. `scheduled_at` (RFC 3339) delays the first batch. The service checks for due launches about every 30 seconds, so the start can be up to that late. A `rollout` call before the time does nothing.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2,
         "scheduled_at":"2026-12-01T03:00:00Z","name":"night wave"}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The schedule survives a restart and runs on whichever replica currently holds the leader role, so a scheduled launch is dispatched once even with several replicas.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Require a version before updating [#require-a-version-before-updating]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Not run here. A pack can require that a device already carries another pack, or a module, at a minimum version. The rule lives on the pack you launch. Devices that fail it are left out, and the dry run lists them:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X PUT $P/preconditions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"preconditions":[{"required_distribution_set_name":"base-os","min_version":"1.0.0"}]}'
  curl -s -X POST "$API/groups/$GROUP/launch?dry_run=true" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"distribution_set_name":"water-panel","workflow_type":"direct","rollout_type":"fixed","rollout_value":2}' | jq -c .precondition_failures
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Each failure names the `device_id`, the `distribution_set_name` (and `module_key` for a module rule), the `current_version` the device has (empty if none) and the `required` constraint, for example `>=1.0.0`. Use `required_module_key` with a `type:name` value to require a module instead. `force_preconditions: true` in the launch body deploys to every device anyway and records the failures.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Update one device to a version [#update-one-device-to-a-version]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Not run here. `force-version` launches a single device to an exact pack version, outside any campaign, and answers `202`. The device must be a member of the pack's group:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/devices/dev-002/force-version -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"distribution_set_id\":\"$PACK\",\"version\":\"1.0.0\",\"group_id\":\"$GROUP\",\"workflow\":\"direct\"}"
  # {"status":"dispatched","device_id":"dev-002","distribution_set_id":"...","version":"1.0.0"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Without `workflow`, a `swu` pack uses `phased`. Only the pack's current version can be forced, unless the pack was created with `allow_previous_version_download`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A new version [#a-new-version]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $P/new -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"1.1.0"}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The version must be higher than the current one, and the pack keeps its id. The new version starts as `draft`. The artifact links and the module composition carry over, but the sw-description does not: upload it again. Then build with `selected_artifact_ids` (a build replaces the carried links with the ones you select), after uploading a new artifact version if the file changed.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Encrypt with a shared key [#encrypt-with-a-shared-key]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  One key encrypts the `.swu` for every device. The sw-description must mark the files to encrypt with `encrypted = true;`. Use a separate pack for each encryption variant: a new version inherits the previous version's encryption settings, and a plain build does not clear them. Rebuilding an already built pack with other settings leaves stale fields too. See [Limitations](/docs/platform/updates/limitations).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  This helper creates a pack, uploads a sw-description that marks its file `encrypted = true;`, and uploads the artifact. It prints the artifact id.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  new_enc_pack() {
    local name=$1 p=$API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/$1
    curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d "{\"name\":\"$name\",\"version\":\"1.0.0\",\"group_id\":\"$GROUP\",\"type\":\"rawfile\",\"packaging\":\"swu\"}"
    sed "s/index.html/$name.html/; s/compressed = \"zlib\";/&\n\t\t\tencrypted = true;/" sw-description > sw-$name
    curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST $p/descriptor/upload -F file=@sw-$name
    cp index.html $name.html
    curl -s -X POST $p/artifact/upload -F file=@$name.html -F artifact_name=$name.html -F version=1.0.0 | jq -r .artifact.id
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  SK=http://localhost:10090/symkms/v1
  ARTE=$(new_enc_pack water-panel-enc)
  PE=$API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/water-panel-enc

  KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
  curl -s -X POST $SK/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"user_id\":\"ops\",\"algorithm\":\"AES-256-GCM\",\"key\":\"$KEY\",\"id\":\"fleet-a-shared\"}"
  # {"id":"fleet-a-shared","user_id":"ops","algorithm":"AES-256-GCM","created_at":"..."}

  curl -s -X POST $PE/swu -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"user\":\"ops\",\"encryption_key_name\":\"fleet-a-shared\",\"encryption_alg_name\":\"AES-256-GCM\",\"selected_artifact_ids\":[\"$ARTE\"]}"
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The pack then reports `"encryption_mode":"shared"`. The device needs the same key and algorithm. See [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Encrypt per device [#encrypt-per-device]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Each device gets its own package and key. This is another pack, built with the same helper. The sw-description must mark a file `encrypted = true;`, or the build is refused.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  ARTP=$(new_enc_pack water-panel-pd)
  PP=$API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/water-panel-pd

  for d in dev-001 dev-002 dev-003 dev-004; do
    curl -s -X POST $SK/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d "{\"user_id\":\"ops\",\"algorithm\":\"AES-256-GCM\",\"key\":\"$(openssl rand -hex 32)\",\"id\":\"pd-$d\"}"
    curl -s -X POST $SK/inventory/$d/keys/pd-$d -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"purpose":"firmware-encryption"}'
  done

  curl -s -X POST $PP/swu -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"encryption_alg_name\":\"AES-256-GCM\",\"selected_artifact_ids\":[\"$ARTP\"]}"
  curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets | jq -c '.list[] | select(.name=="water-panel-pd") | {status,encryption_mode,built_device_count,total_device_count}'
  # {"status":"built","encryption_mode":"per-device","built_device_count":4,"total_device_count":4}

  curl -s -o dev-001.swu $PP/swu/download/dev-001     # each device downloads its own file
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If a device has no key at build time, the build still succeeds and the pack records the gap. If **no** device has a key, the build fails instead.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```json
  {"encryption_mode":"per-device","built_device_count":3,"total_device_count":4,
   "uncovered_devices":[{"device_id":"dev-004","reason":"no firmware-encryption key assigned"}]}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A launch on that pack is refused, dry runs included, and `force_preconditions` does not override it:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  {"err":"Cannot create launch: update pack \"water-panel\" is per-device encrypted and only 3 of 4 devices have a package. The rest would fail to download. Missing: dev-004 (no firmware-encryption key assigned). Fix those devices and regenerate the SWU."}   [400]
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Coverage is recorded when the pack is built, so assigning the missing key is not enough. Build the pack again (a new version) with a key for every device.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Sign the package [#sign-the-package]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Add the KMS signing fields to the build body. They need a signing key and certificate in the Lamassu KMS, with `kms_endpoint` and `sign_script_path` set. This request was not run here, because it needs a KMS. See [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  jq -n --arg art "$ART" --arg cert "$(cat signer.pem)" '{
      selected_artifact_ids: [$art],
      signature_key_id: "<kms key id>",
      signature_alg_name: "RSASSA_PSS_SHA_256",
      signature_certificate: $cert }' \
    | curl -s -X POST $P/swu -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @-
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                                  | Cause and fix                                                                                                                 |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `409` on `artifact/upload` or `artifact/link`                            | The pack version is already `built`. Create a new version with `POST .../new`                                                 |
  | `409` on `POST .../distribution-sets`                                    | A pack with that name already exists in the group                                                                             |
  | `400 version ... must be greater than the current latest version`        | An artifact name is global and its version must increase. Upload with a higher `version`                                      |
  | The build fails with an empty binaries directory                         | The build received no `selected_artifact_ids`                                                                                 |
  | `400` creating a launch: pack has not been built                         | Build it first. A pack in `build_failed` is not launchable either                                                             |
  | `400 ... is per-device encrypted and only N of M devices have a package` | Some devices have no `firmware-encryption` key. Assign keys and build a new version                                           |
  | `rollout` answers `400` with `rolls out automatically`                   | The launch has `auto` on and already started. Wait for the approval threshold, or pause it                                    |
  | `rollout` answers `400` with `test device ... failed`                    | The canary failed. Resume the launch to retry it, or cancel                                                                   |
  | `413` on an upload                                                       | The file is over `max_artifact_size_mb` (10 GiB by default), or the gateway or ingress limit in front of the service is lower |
  | `501` on a module route                                                  | Native mode has no per-module deliverables. Build the pack instead                                                            |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Next steps [#next-steps]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * [Update flow with curl, hawkBit backend](/docs/platform/updates/guides/hawkbit-curl)
  * [Connect a device](/docs/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device) for what a real device must implement
  * [API reference](/docs/platform/updates/reference/api)
  * [Troubleshooting](/docs/platform/updates/troubleshooting)
</div>


# Publish and roll out an update (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  This guide takes one update from nothing to devices: create an update pack, attach an artifact and a `sw-description`, build the deliverable, create a launch (a campaign in the dashboard) and release it batch by batch. The requests use native mode. hawkBit mode builds and creates packs in a different order, described in [hawkBit mode](#hawkbit-mode). To do the same through screens, follow [Use the dashboard](/docs/platform/updates/guides/dashboard).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  flowchart LR
    A[Create pack] --> B[Upload sw-description and artifact]
    B --> C[Build the .swu]
    C --> D[Create launch]
    D --> E[Roll out batches]
    E --> F[Verify devices]
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Before you begin [#before-you-begin]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * The [stack is running](/docs/platform/updates/getting-started) and `curl localhost:10090/health` answers.
  * A Lamassu IoT device group that contains the devices you want to update. Its ID is `$GROUP`. A pack belongs to one group and can only be launched to that group's devices.
  * The binary to deliver and, for an SWU pack, a `sw-description` file.
  * Devices that can receive the update. See [Connect a device](/docs/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  API=http://localhost:10090/updates/v1
  GROUP=<your-group-id>
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The service has no built-in authentication, so these examples send none. Put a gateway that authenticates callers in front of it: see [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  1. Create the pack [#1-create-the-pack]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name":"my-firmware","version":"1.0.0","group_id":"'$GROUP'","type":"firmware","packaging":"swu"}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The response is `201` with the pack, including its `id`. A pack starts as `draft`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Field                             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                     |
  | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `name`                            | Required. Unique within the group; a duplicate answers `409`. Native mode uses it as a path segment, so it may contain only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` (no spaces) |
  | `version`                         | Required. Strict semver `x.y.z`, set by you                                                                                                                               |
  | `group_id`                        | Required in the body. Use the same value as in the path                                                                                                                   |
  | `type`                            | `rawfile` or `firmware`. Recorded on the pack and sent to the device in the job; the dashboard also offers `both` and `other`. Not validated at creation                  |
  | `packaging`                       | `swu` (default) or `non-swu`. A `non-swu` pack delivers its files as a `.tar.gz` and uses the `download-install` workflow                                                 |
  | `allow_previous_version_download` | Optional. Lets devices download older versions of the pack                                                                                                                |
  | `preconditions`                   | Optional rules a device must meet to receive the pack. See [Concepts](/docs/platform/updates/concepts)                                                                    |
  | `modules`                         | **hawkBit mode only**: the pack's composition, as built catalog modules. Native ignores it                                                                                |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  2. Upload the sw-description and the artifact [#2-upload-the-sw-description-and-the-artifact]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `sw-description` is an SWUpdate file that lists what the device installs. Its format is SWUpdate's, and the [SWUpdate documentation](https://sbabic.github.io/swupdate/sw-description.html) is the reference. When the service builds the `.swu`, `swugenerator` reads this file and the staged binaries, so the `filename` of every image must be the name of an uploaded file. A minimal one:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  software =
  {
  	version = "1.0.0";
  	description = "My panel";
  	hardware-compatibility: [ "1.0" ];
  	images: (
  		{
  			filename = "rootfs.img";        # the uploaded file's name
  			path = "/web/index.html";
  			type = "rawfile";
  			compressed = "zlib";            # swugenerator compresses the file
  			properties: {
  				decompressed-size = "<bytes>";  # set it whenever compressed is set
  			};
  		}
  	);
  }
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `swugenerator` fills in the final `filename` (with `.zlib` added, and `.enc` for encrypted files), the `sha256` and, for encrypted files, the `ivt` property. For an encrypted build, add `encrypted = true;` to each image that must be encrypted. Two rules cause most failures:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * `encrypted = true` must appear only in a build that supplies a key (the build fails without one), and a per-device build refuses a description in which no image has it.
  * Compressed images need `decompressed-size`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If you build the `.swu` yourself and upload it as a prebuilt deliverable, you fill in `sha256` and `ivt` yourself, and the `sha256` is over the bytes the device downloads, because SWUpdate hashes before it decrypts.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  # The sw-description (multipart field "file")
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/my-firmware/descriptor/upload \
    -F file=@sw-description

  # The binary (multipart: "file", plus "artifact_name" and "version")
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/my-firmware/artifact/upload \
    -F file=@rootfs.img -F artifact_name=rootfs.img -F version=1.0.0
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * `artifact_name` defaults to the file name without its extension. `version` is optional; when you upload a new file under an existing `artifact_name` it must be strictly higher than the highest version already stored under that name.
  * The artifact is stored as a global artifact and linked to this pack. The response contains its `id`. To reuse an artifact that is already uploaded, link it with `POST .../artifact/link` and `{"artifact_id":"<id>"}`.
  * The largest accepted file is `max_artifact_size_mb` (10 GiB by default). A bigger upload answers `413`.
  * Once the pack is built, uploads and links answer `409`: create a new version first.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Compose a pack from several modules (optional) [#compose-a-pack-from-several-modules-optional]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A native pack is a composition of software modules: one `os` module plus any number of `application` modules. A pack with no declared modules behaves as a single implicit `os` module that owns the artifacts you uploaded above. To add an application module and give it its own files:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/my-firmware/modules \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"type":"application","name":"telemetry","version":"1.0.0"}'

  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/my-firmware/modules/application:telemetry/artifact/upload \
    -F file=@telemetry.bin -F artifact_name=telemetry
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The module key is `<type>:<name>`. Native still builds one `.swu` for the whole pack, from every module's artifacts and the pack's single `sw-description`. You can also compose from a module that already exists with `POST .../modules/import`; in native mode that copies the module, while in hawkBit mode it links the same module. See [Concepts](/docs/platform/updates/concepts) for the model.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  3. Build the deliverable [#3-build-the-deliverable]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/my-firmware/swu \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"selected_artifact_ids":["<artifact id>"]}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `selected_artifact_ids` is what puts artifacts into the build: only the listed artifacts are staged. With an empty list the build fails because no binaries were staged, and the pack becomes `build_failed`. Take the ID from the artifact upload response, or from `GET $API/artifacts`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The body above builds an unencrypted, unsigned `.swu`. To sign or encrypt, add fields as described in [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * For a `non-swu` pack, call `POST .../package` instead of `.../swu`. With no `selected_artifact_ids` it packages the artifacts linked to the pack.
  * To deliver a file you built elsewhere, upload it to `POST .../swu/upload` (or `.../package/upload`) as a multipart `file`. It is stored and served unchanged, so it must already be signed and encrypted the way your devices expect. Native mode only.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  When the build succeeds, the pack becomes `built` and its artifacts and composition are immutable. If it fails, the pack becomes `build_failed` and `last_build_error` holds the reason: fix the input and build again. A build that runs while another one holds the same pack answers `409`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  4. Create the launch [#4-create-the-launch]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{
          "distribution_set_name":"my-firmware",
          "workflow_type":"direct",
          "rollout_type":"percentage",
          "rollout_value":10,
          "test_device_id":"<canary-device-id>",
          "name":"my-firmware 1.0.0 first wave"
        }'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The launch targets every device of the group at the moment you create it, and it needs a built pack. The response is `201` with `launch_id`, `precondition_failures`, `forced`, and, in hawkBit mode, `superseded_devices` and `never_seen_devices`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Field                                                                     | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `distribution_set_name`, `workflow_type`, `rollout_type`, `rollout_value` | Required. `rollout_value` must be greater than 0                                                                                                                                                   |
  | `rollout_type`                                                            | `percentage` of the group per batch, or `fixed` (a device count). Any value other than `percentage` is read as a count                                                                             |
  | `workflow_type`                                                           | Native: `direct`, `phased`, `download-install`, or the full name of another workflow registered in WFX (`GET $API/workflows`). hawkBit: `phased` creates a soft action, anything else a forced one |
  | `test_device_id`                                                          | Optional canary: a member of the group that is updated first and must succeed before any other device is touched                                                                                   |
  | `auto`, `approval_threshold`, `error_threshold`                           | Optional. `auto` releases later batches by itself. Both thresholds are percentages from 0 to 100                                                                                                   |
  | `scheduled_at`                                                            | Optional RFC 3339 time. The first batch is delayed until then                                                                                                                                      |
  | `name`, `description`, `weight`                                           | Optional. `name` defaults to the pack's name. `weight` (0 to 1000) is stored but nothing reads it                                                                                                  |
  | `force_preconditions`                                                     | Deploy to devices that fail the pack's preconditions anyway. The failures are still recorded                                                                                                       |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Choose the workflow to match the pack:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * Use `direct` for SWU packs unless you drive WFX yourself. The `phased` workflow has steps that WFX or an operator must confirm, and this service does not advance them. A `phased` launch stays at its first state until someone confirms it through WFX.
  * For a `non-swu` pack set `workflow_type` to `download-install`. The launch uses the value you give verbatim, so `direct` would run the SWU workflow and the update would look stuck after the device finished.
  * In hawkBit mode there is no WFX. The choice is hawkBit's install mode.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  If the pack has preconditions, preview who qualifies before creating anything by adding `?dry_run=true` to the same request. It answers `200` with `qualifying_devices`, `precondition_failures`, `superseded_devices` and `never_seen_devices`, and creates nothing.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  **Approval and error thresholds.** With `auto: true`, the next batch is released once at least `approval_threshold` percent of the current batch has succeeded (0 means the whole batch). In native mode the campaign is cancelled when `error_threshold` percent of all its devices have failed; in hawkBit mode it stops when more than that percentage of a batch fails. A failed canary pauses a native campaign instead: resume it to retry the canary.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Take the launch ID from the response. It is `$LAUNCH` below.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  5. Roll it out [#5-roll-it-out]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/rollout
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Without `auto`, each call dispatches the next batch (the canary first, if you set one). With `auto: true`, call it once to start the first batch: the service then releases the later batches itself as the approval threshold is met, and further calls answer `400`. If the launch has a future `scheduled_at`, the call is accepted but does nothing: the service starts it by itself at that time (native checks every 30 seconds; hawkBit's own scheduler starts the rollout).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A native launch moves through these statuses:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> running
    running --> paused: pause or failed canary
    paused --> running: resume
    running --> completed: every device processed
    running --> cancelled: cancel or error threshold
    paused --> cancelled: cancel
    completed --> running: retry failed
    cancelled --> running: retry failed
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  You can steer a launch while it runs:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Action                      | Request                                        | Effect                                                                                                                                                    |
  | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Pause                       | `POST $API/groups/$GROUP/launch/$LAUNCH/pause` | No further batches until resumed. Devices already in flight finish                                                                                        |
  | Resume                      | `POST .../resume`                              | Native: an automatic campaign releases its next batch at once if the current one already met the threshold, and resuming after a failed canary retries it |
  | Retry failed devices        | `POST .../retry-failed`                        | Re-queues the failed devices and dispatches them. Answers `400` when there is none                                                                        |
  | Cancel (terminal)           | `POST .../cancel`                              | Pending devices are not updated                                                                                                                           |
  | Mark complete (terminal)    | `POST .../complete`                            | Not available in hawkBit mode                                                                                                                             |
  | Read or change the strategy | `GET`, `PUT .../strategy`                      | Changing it is not available in hawkBit mode                                                                                                              |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In hawkBit mode a rollout can only be paused after it has started dispatching.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Verify the result [#verify-the-result]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  # The launches of the group, each with its per-status device counts
  curl -s $API/groups/$GROUP/launch

  # One job per device of a launch
  curl -s $API/launch/$LAUNCH/jobs

  # What a given device now carries
  curl -s $API/devices/<device-id>/distribution-set-inventory
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The launch list answers `{"list":[...],"next":"..."}`. A launch is done when `pending_count` and `active_count` are zero; a native launch then sets its `status` to `completed` by itself. Devices end as `completed` (job state `ACTIVATED`, or `INSTALLED` for `non-swu`) or `failed` (`TERMINATED`).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Ship the next version [#ship-the-next-version]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A built pack version is immutable. To change it, create the next version, upload what changed and build again:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $API/groups/$GROUP/distribution-sets/my-firmware/new \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"1.1.0"}'
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The version must be strictly higher than the current one. The new version starts unbuilt and carries the current artifacts forward.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To update one device to an exact version without a campaign, use `POST $API/devices/<device-id>/force-version` with `{"distribution_set_id":"<pack id>","version":"1.1.0"}`; in native mode it creates a one-device launch and defaults to the `phased` workflow for SWU packs (`download-install` for `non-swu`) unless you pass a `workflow`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit mode [#hawkbit-mode]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit packs are assembled from built catalog modules, so the pack-side steps 2 and 3 move to the catalog:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  1. Create the module: `POST $API/softwaremodules` with `type` (`os` or `application`), `name`, `version` and a `delivery_intent`: `swu-build`, `swu-prebuilt` or `raw`. `undecided` is accepted, but a module cannot join a pack until you choose.
  2. Upload the file with `POST $API/softwaremodules/by-id/<id>/artifacts`. For `swu-build`, also upload the `sw-description` to `.../descriptor` and call `POST $API/softwaremodules/by-id/<id>/build`. For `swu-prebuilt`, uploading the `.swu` is the build. For `raw`, call `.../build` to make the files the deliverable; signing and encryption are optional.
  3. Create the pack with `"modules":[{"source_module_id":"<id>"}]`. It is created already built.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Then continue at step 4. Details, including the delivery intents, are in [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode), and a full request sequence is in [hawkBit curl guide](/docs/platform/updates/guides/hawkbit-curl).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                                                   | Likely cause                                                                                                                                                                                      |
  | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | A call returns `501 Not Implemented`                                                      | The active backend does not support it. Check [Capabilities](/docs/platform/updates/reference/capabilities)                                                                                       |
  | `400` "has not been built yet" when creating a launch                                     | The pack is `draft` or `build_failed`. Build it first                                                                                                                                             |
  | `400` about devices with no package                                                       | A per-device encrypted pack was built for only some devices. The message names the devices missing a key; fix them and rebuild                                                                    |
  | `400` "group has no devices to launch to"                                                 | The group has no members, or none qualify. Check the group's criteria and the pack's preconditions                                                                                                |
  | Build returns an error about `encrypted = true`                                           | A per-device build needs at least one image marked `encrypted = true` in the `sw-description`                                                                                                     |
  | SWU build fails with "failed to read binaries directory" or "binaries directory is empty" | Nothing was staged: no `selected_artifact_ids` in the build body                                                                                                                                  |
  | `409` on upload, link or build                                                            | The version is already built (create a new version), or another request is building the same pack                                                                                                 |
  | `413` on upload                                                                           | The file is larger than `max_artifact_size_mb`                                                                                                                                                    |
  | Rollout answers `400` "paused" or "rolls out automatically"                               | Resume the launch, or let the automatic campaign release its own batches                                                                                                                          |
  | Launch stays `running` with no device progress (hawkBit)                                  | Devices never contacted hawkBit. A rollout group cannot advance until its devices poll                                                                                                            |
  | Devices cannot download the `.swu` (native)                                               | `update_domain` is not reachable from the device, or is not the full `.../updates/v1/` base with a trailing slash. The download URL is fixed when the pack is built, so rebuild after changing it |
  | Create-pack fails in hawkBit mode                                                         | A pack with that name already exists in the group (`409`), a module is not built or not linked by `source_module_id`, or the name and version of an earlier module are reserved. Bump the version |
  | A `non-swu` launch runs the SWU states                                                    | The launch was created with `workflow_type: direct`. Use `download-install`                                                                                                                       |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Next steps [#next-steps]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Cards>
    <Card title="Concepts" href="/docs/platform/updates/concepts" description="Packs, modules, launches, workflows and preconditions." />

    <Card title="Native curl guide" href="/docs/platform/updates/guides/native-curl" description="Every request of the native flow, in order." />

    <Card title="API reference" href="/docs/platform/updates/reference/api" description="All routes, bodies and status codes." />
  </Cards>
</div>


# hawkBit mode (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In `hawkbit` mode, Lamassu Updates serves the same `/updates/v1` API on top of an [Eclipse hawkBit](https://www.eclipse.org/hawkbit/) server instead of its own Postgres, WFX and SymKMS-based backend. The service becomes an **adapter**: hawkBit owns packs, modules, rollouts and jobs and is read live on every request, and devices talk to hawkBit directly.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Use it when hawkBit is already your fleet's update backend, or to compare the two backends. To choose between them, see the [overview](/docs/platform/updates/overview).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```mermaid
  flowchart LR
    operator["Dashboard / API clients"] --> adapter["Lamassu Updates<br/>(hawkbit mode)"]
    adapter -->|Management API| hawkbit["Eclipse hawkBit"]
    adapter --> pg[("Postgres<br/>updates")]
    adapter -.->|DMS API, KMS, SymKMS| lamassu["Lamassu IoT"]
    device["Device (SWUpdate)"] -->|DDI poll| hawkbit
    device -->|artifact URL| adapter
    adapter -.->|302 signed URL| device
    device -->|signed GET| s3[("S3 store")]
    hawkbit -->|stores artifacts| s3
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Prerequisites [#prerequisites]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * A reachable hawkBit server (1.x) and its Management API credentials.
  * Postgres for this service. See [What lives where](#what-lives-where).
  * Devices that poll hawkBit through SWUpdate's `suricatta` module. With `dms_endpoint` set, the service creates the hawkBit targets of a group's devices and tags them itself (see [Devices and targets](#devices-and-targets)). Without it, you register and tag them in hawkBit.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Enable it [#enable-it]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```yaml
  mode: hawkbit
  hawkbit:
    base_url: "http://hawkbit:8080"      # hawkBit's Management API
    username: "admin"
    password: "<hawkbit admin password>"
    tenant: ""                           # DDI tenant path segment; defaults to DEFAULT
  storage:                               # required: Postgres of this service
    provider: postgres
    hostname: postgres
    port: 5432
    username: postgres
    password: "<password>"
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `mode` is `native` when unset, so existing configurations are unaffected. Startup fails if `hawkbit.base_url` or `storage.hostname` is empty. An unreachable hawkBit does not stop startup: it shows up as errors on requests.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  To build deliverables in this mode, add the pieces you need on top. All are read once at start-up:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | You want                               | Set                                                                                                           |
  | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `swu-build` modules (assembled `.swu`) | `swugenerator_path`                                                                                           |
  | Signing with the Lamassu KMS           | also `sign_script_path` and `kms_endpoint` (raw modules need only `kms_endpoint`)                             |
  | Shared-key encryption                  | `symkms_endpoint`, plus the `symkms` block or `sym_keys_dir` so the process registers the `/symkms/v1` routes |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  See the [configuration reference](/docs/platform/updates/reference/configuration) and [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption). Without these keys, `GET /updates/v1/capabilities` reports `artifact_encryption: false` and the dashboard hides the encryption selector.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Callout type="info" title="Which port is the adapter on?">
    The API listens on `app.server.port`, and clients choose it. The dashboard reads its API URL from `LAMASSU_UPDATES_API`, so point that at the instance that runs the mode you want. If you run a native and a `hawkbit` instance side by side, give them different ports, and set each instance's `symkms_endpoint` to **its own** port: it points at the same process.
  </Callout>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Run it locally [#run-it-locally]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The repository's `docker-compose.yml` starts a hawkBit (host port `8090`, backed by the `hawkbit` Postgres database) and the Postgres both services use:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
