  | Key                                                            | Default                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `enabled`                                                      | `false`                   | Turns the feature on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
  | `public_endpoint`                                              | the storage `s3_endpoint` | Origin of the store **as devices reach it**, without a path (for example the gateway that publishes the bucket). It is what gets signed: the signature covers the `Host` header, so a URL signed for an in-cluster address is refused when a device fetches it through the gateway. Required unless devices reach the store at its own endpoint (for example AWS S3). |
  | `ttl`                                                          | `60s`                     | How long a URL can **start** a download. Between `1s` and 7 days. A transfer already under way is not cut when it expires.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
  | `min_remaining`                                                | `min(25s, ttl/2)`         | A URL already signed for the same object is handed out again while it has at least this much validity left, so a retry or resume never gets a URL about to expire. Negative signs a fresh URL on every request. Must be lower than `ttl`.                                                                                                                             |
  | `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key` (or the `_file` variants) | none                      | The credential that signs. **Required, and it must be a read-only credential different from the storage one.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  At start-up the service refuses to run when the signing credential is the storage credential, when it can write to the bucket (it probes with a write), when the store rejects it (it waits up to 2 minutes for the store to accept it), or when `encryption.type` is not `none` (devices would receive ciphertext). If the store cannot be asked at all, it logs a warning and continues. The device must still be able to resolve and reach `public_endpoint`. See [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security#presigned-download-urls).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkbit block [#hawkbit-block]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Used only when `mode: hawkbit`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Key                                    | Default            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
  | -------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `hawkbit.base_url`                     | none (required)    | hawkBit Management API root, for example `http://hawkbit:8080`. Startup fails if it is empty. Calls time out after 30 s; artifact transfers after 6 h.                                                                                         |
  | `hawkbit.username`, `hawkbit.password` | none               | Management API Basic Auth credentials.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
  | `hawkbit.tenant`                       | `DEFAULT`          | DDI tenant path segment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
  | `hawkbit.ddi_url`                      | `hawkbit.base_url` | hawkBit's DDI root **as devices reach it** (for example `https://updates.example.com/api/hawkbit-ddi`). It is used to build the download URLs devices receive, and its path becomes the prefix of the DDI download route this service serves.  |
  | `hawkbit.artifact_store`               | none               | Same shape as the [blob storage blocks](#blob-storage-blocks): `storage` must point to the bucket and `s3_prefix` of hawkBit's S3 artifact plugin, and `presign` enables signed downloads. Without it, artifacts are streamed through hawkBit. |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `storage` (Postgres) block is also required in `hawkbit` mode.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Environment variables [#environment-variables]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Any key of the file can be overridden by an environment variable: the name is the key path in upper case with dots replaced by underscores. `KMS_ENDPOINT` overrides `kms_endpoint`, `STORAGE_PASSWORD` overrides `storage.password` and `BUILDS_PRESIGN_TTL` overrides `builds.presign.ttl`. The key must exist in the file (an empty value is enough): the loader only considers keys it has read from it.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Variables the code reads besides these overrides:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Variable                    | Description                                                                                                                                              |
  | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `OTA_CONFIG_FILE`           | Configuration file path.                                                                                                                                 |
  | `POD_NAME`, `POD_NAMESPACE` | Identity and namespace for Kubernetes leader election. The Helm chart sets them. If unset, the hostname and the service-account namespace file are used. |
  | `TMPDIR`                    | Where uploads and builds write temporary files (Go's temporary directory).                                                                               |
  | `SERVER_PORT`               | Used only by the health check of the Docker image to find the port. Default `10090`.                                                                     |
  | `AWS_*`                     | The AWS default credential chain, when an S3 or AWS KMS block has no explicit credential.                                                                |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  For Docker Compose, the `.env` file is read by `docker-compose.yml`, not by the service: `HOST_IP`, `HAWKBIT_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `HAWKBIT_ARTIFACT_STORAGE` and the `HAWKBIT_ARTIFACT_S3_*` and `LOCAL_S3_*` variables. See `.env.example` in the repository.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Callout type="warn" title="Debug logging prints the configuration">
    With `app.logs.level: debug`, the service writes the whole loaded configuration to the log at start-up, including `storage.password`, `encryption.local_key`, S3 keys and `hawkbit.password`. In `native` mode the `storage` block, password included, is also printed to standard output at every start, whatever the log level. Use `info` or higher anywhere logs are stored or shared, and keep secrets in a secret store, not in the file (see the `*_file` credentials above).
  </Callout>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Minimal configurations [#minimal-configurations]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `native` mode needs the database, the endpoints it calls and storage paths. Start from `config-docker.yml`:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```yaml
  app:
    logs: {level: info}
    server: {listen_address: "0.0.0.0", port: 10090}
  storage:
    provider: postgres
    hostname: postgres
    port: 5432
    username: postgres
    password: "<password>"
  dms_endpoint: "http://<lamassu>/api/devmanager"
  kms_endpoint: "http://<lamassu>/api/kms/v1"
  wfx_endpoint: "http://custom-wfx:8081/"
  update_domain: "http://updates:10090/updates/v1/"
  symkms_endpoint: "http://updates:10090"
  update_files_base_dir: "/data/update_files"
  sym_keys_dir: "/data/symmetric_keys"
  sign_script_path: "/app/sign_kms.sh"
  workflow_file: "/app/wfx/workflow/dau/wfx.workflow.dau.direct.yml"
  symkms:
    storage: {type: local, local_dir: "/data/symmetric_keys"}
    encryption: {type: none}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `hawkbit` mode needs `mode: hawkbit`, `hawkbit.base_url`, the Management API credentials and the `storage` block. Add the build settings only if you want builds. The keys below are the ones `config-hawkbit.yml` uses:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```yaml
  mode: hawkbit
  hawkbit:
    base_url: "http://hawkbit:8080"
    username: "admin"
    password: "<hawkbit admin password>"
  swugenerator_path: "/usr/local/bin/swugenerator"   # builds .swu modules
  sign_script_path: "/app/sign_kms.sh"               # with kms_endpoint: signing
  kms_endpoint: "http://<lamassu>/api/kms/v1"
  symkms_endpoint: "http://localhost:10090"          # with the symkms block: encryption
  sym_keys_dir: "/data/symmetric_keys"
  symkms:
    storage: {type: local, local_dir: "/data/symmetric_keys"}
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In `hawkbit` mode the SymKMS routes are registered only when `symkms.storage.type` or `sym_keys_dir` is set. With `symkms_endpoint` set but neither of those, every key lookup would be answered `404` by the service itself.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  SymKMS as its own process [#symkms-as-its-own-process]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `cmd/symkms` binary runs SymKMS alone. Its configuration has only `app` (as above), `symkms` (a storage block) and `sym_keys_dir`. Its key directory defaults to `/data/symmetric_keys` when neither `symkms.storage.local_dir` nor `sym_keys_dir` is set. It serves `/symkms/v1/*` but no `/health` route, and it has the same lack of authentication as the monolith: see [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Related pages [#related-pages]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * [Operations](/docs/platform/updates/operations) for the Helm values, scaling and backups.
  * [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode) for what changes in that backend.
  * [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption) for the keys behind `kms_endpoint` and `symkms`.
  * [Troubleshooting](/docs/platform/updates/troubleshooting) for start-up errors.
</div>


# Security (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/security)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Lamassu Updates delegates authentication, authorization and TLS to the platform gateway in front of it. This page lists what the service itself enforces, what it does not, and what to configure around it. Read it before exposing the service beyond a trusted network.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Summary [#summary]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Area                            | State                                                                                                                                                                 |
  | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Authentication of API callers   | **None in the service.** Every route is open to anyone who can reach the port. The gateway must authenticate.                                                         |
  | Authorization                   | **No roles or per-group permissions.** The service only does structural checks (see [What the service checks](#what-the-service-checks)). The gateway must authorize. |
  | TLS and mTLS (inbound)          | **Not implemented.** The service always serves plain HTTP.                                                                                                            |
  | TLS to other systems            | Postgres: always `sslmode=disable`. KMS: not verified in `native` mode, and the SWU signer script uses `curl -k`. See [Outbound connections](#outbound-connections).  |
  | CORS                            | Any origin and any header are allowed.                                                                                                                                |
  | Rate limiting, security headers | None added by the service.                                                                                                                                            |
  | Package signing                 | Available, through the Lamassu KMS. See [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption).                                                      |
  | Package encryption              | Available: shared key or per-device key.                                                                                                                              |
  | At-rest encryption              | Available for artifacts, builds and keys, through the `encryption` block of each storage block.                                                                       |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `cert_file`, `key_file` and `authentication.mutual_tls.*` keys exist in the configuration structs but are not read, so setting them does nothing.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  What to put in front of it [#what-to-put-in-front-of-it]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Run the service behind a gateway or reverse proxy that:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  1. **Terminates TLS** between clients and the service.
  2. **Authenticates and authorizes** callers: operators for the API, and devices for the download routes. A device must only reach its own download paths, so match the device certificate to the `:deviceID` (or `:controllerId`) in the path.
  3. **Restricts the dangerous routes** to the callers that need them (see below).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Keep the service on a private network. Devices need to reach only the download routes and, in `native` mode, the WFX **client** listener. In `hawkbit` mode they talk to hawkBit (and to the signed-URL store) and not to this service, except for the artifact download route described in [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode#artifact-storage-and-downloads).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  WFX has a client listener (`8080` in Compose, published as `9080`) and a management listener (`8081`, published as `9081`). Lamassu Updates authenticates neither. Devices need the client listener only: do not expose the management port to devices or untrusted networks.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  How the service identifies itself to others [#how-the-service-identifies-itself-to-others]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The service does not forward the caller's identity. Calls to the Lamassu Device Manager and the KMS carry the fixed header `X-Principal-ID: admin-mode`, which the platform's authorization layer accepts for internal callers and which the platform gateway strips from external traffic. The value is not configurable, so point `dms_endpoint` and `kms_endpoint` at internal service addresses, not at a public gateway path that would reject or forward it. SymKMS calls from the service carry no credential.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Routes to restrict [#routes-to-restrict]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Route                                                                 | Why                                                                                                                         |
  | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `GET /symkms/v1/:keyID/raw`                                           | Returns raw key material.                                                                                                   |
  | `GET /symkms/v1/inventory/:deviceID/key`                              | Returns a device's raw key material. The Updates service uses it during a per-device build.                                 |
  | `POST /symkms/v1/`, `DELETE /symkms/v1/:keyID`, key assignment routes | Create, delete and assign encryption keys.                                                                                  |
  | `POST /symkms/v1/encrypt`, `/decrypt`, `/mac`                         | Use stored keys on arbitrary data.                                                                                          |
  | `PUT /updates/v1/jobs/:jobID/transition`                              | Forges a job state change with no ownership check. Registered only when `enable_test_endpoints` is `true`: keep it `false`. |
  | Every `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` of `/updates/v1`                     | Build, launch, cancel and delete. Restrict them to operators.                                                               |
  | `GET` of artifacts, descriptors and `artifacts-archive`               | Expose firmware sources and sw-descriptions.                                                                                |
  | Download routes with `:deviceID`                                      | Per-device builds are encrypted with that device's key, but the route itself checks nothing about who asks.                 |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  What the service checks [#what-the-service-checks]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  These are defence in depth, not a substitute for the gateway:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * A launch is addressed under its group: an operation on a launch through another group's path answers `404`, exactly as for a missing launch, and changes nothing.
  * Approval and error thresholds must be between 0 and 100.
  * In `native` mode, pack, group and device identifiers used in paths are validated so they cannot escape the storage directories, and a per-device pack never falls back to the shared build for a device.
  * An upload under a `.swu` name must really be a SWU: other content is refused with `400`.
  * An uploaded file larger than `max_artifact_size_mb` is refused with `413`.
  * In `hawkbit` mode the DDI artifact route serves a file only if the module is assigned to or installed on that device.
  * Anything that changes a built version is refused (`409`): versions are immutable.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Presigned download URLs [#presigned-download-urls]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  With `presign.enabled`, a download is answered `302` to a short-lived URL of the S3 store. The service authorizes the caller first (the gateway for the static route and, in `hawkbit` mode, the device's assignment); the store then checks only the signature, so **the URL is a bearer capability**: whoever holds it can fetch that one object until it expires. The design keeps that acceptable:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * The TTL is short (default 60 s). It bounds when a GET can **start**: a transfer in progress finishes after expiry, and a device that retries or resumes goes back to the static endpoint for a fresh URL. A URL already signed for the same object is reused while it has `min_remaining` validity left (default `min(25s, ttl/2)`); it grants no more than a fresh one.
  * The signing credential must be **read-only** and different from the storage credential. At start-up the service probes with a write and refuses to run if the credential can write, is the storage's own, or is rejected by the store. A signature covers the method and the key, so a URL cannot be turned into a `PUT` or aimed at another object.
  * The signed host is the store's **public** origin (`presign.public_endpoint`), because the signature covers the `Host` header.
  * It cannot be combined with at-rest encryption of the same store (devices would receive ciphertext).
  * Redirect responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`. `HEAD` requests are answered by the service, not redirected. If signing fails, the service streams the file instead of failing the update.
  * Rotate the signing credential by updating the files named by `access_key_id_file` and `secret_access_key_file`: they are re-read every minute.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The store itself must be reachable by devices at the public endpoint, and should accept only the read-only credential on the prefix it serves. Do not publish the store's console or S3 API with default credentials.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Outbound connections [#outbound-connections]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Connection             | Transport security                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
  | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Postgres               | `sslmode=disable`, not configurable. Keep the database on a private network.                                                                                                                                                                            |
  | Lamassu Device Manager | The Lamassu platform SDK client with its default settings.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | Lamassu KMS            | `native` mode: certificate verification is **skipped** for the service's own calls, and the SWU signer script uses `curl -k`. `hawkbit` mode: the service's calls verify the certificate, the script still does not. Use an internal address you trust. |
  | SymKMS                 | The scheme of `symkms_endpoint` (normally the service itself, over plain HTTP in the examples), with no credential. Raw key material crosses this connection: keep it on `localhost` or a private network.                                              |
  | hawkBit Management API | HTTP Basic with `hawkbit.username` and `hawkbit.password`. Use HTTPS.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
  | WFX                    | The scheme of `wfx_endpoint` (plain HTTP in the examples), to the management listener.                                                                                                                                                                  |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Secrets [#secrets]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * `encryption.local_key`, S3 credentials and database passwords must come from a secret store, not from a file in the repository. The example configurations contain development values only. Prefer the `*_file` form of S3 and presign credentials, which the service re-reads every minute.
  * The Helm chart renders all of `config` into a ConfigMap. See [Operations](/docs/platform/updates/operations#secrets-with-helm). Override its placeholder database password.
  * With `app.logs.level: debug` the service logs the whole configuration, secrets included, and in `native` mode it prints the `storage` block (with its password) to standard output at every start. Use `info` or higher in any environment whose logs are stored.
  * A lost `encryption.local_key` makes everything stored with it unreadable. See [Backup and restore](/docs/platform/updates/operations#backup-and-restore).
  * Signing keys stay in the Lamassu KMS: the service never holds the private key. Device encryption keys do live in SymKMS (optionally encrypted at rest), because packages must be encrypted with them.
  * The container image does not drop privileges. Set a `securityContext` that suits your cluster.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  hawkBit mode [#hawkbit-mode]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * The Management API user is a full administrator of hawkBit. Change the default (`admin`) credential, keep the API off the device network and serve it over HTTPS.
  * Devices authenticate to hawkBit, not to this service. hawkBit 1.1.0 has no anonymous mode: enable a target security token, a gateway token or the reverse-proxy header authenticator, and for the last restrict which addresses may set its headers. Leaving device authentication off, which is acceptable only on a throw-away test stack, lets anything that can reach hawkBit impersonate a device. See [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode#device-authentication-in-production).
  * hawkBit does not encrypt artifacts at rest. Enable default encryption in the bucket, or use encrypted (shared-key) packages.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Request limits [#request-limits]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  A request body can be up to `max_artifact_size_mb` plus 1 MiB (10 GiB by default), and a request can take up to 6 hours, so large uploads work. Streamed uploads use temporary disk under `TMPDIR`. Apply tighter limits at the gateway for callers that are not trusted: there is no rate limiting in the service.
</div>


# Signing and encryption (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  This page explains how Lamassu Updates protects what it delivers: which keys sign and encrypt a package, how to configure them, and what each backend supports. There are three independent layers.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Layer              | Protects                                                                 | Configured in                                                                                                           |
  | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Package signing    | That the package came from you and is unmodified                         | A signing key and certificate in the Lamassu KMS, plus `kms_endpoint` and `sign_script_path`                            |
  | Package encryption | The contents of the package in transit and on the device's download path | The build request, plus a key in SymKMS                                                                                 |
  | At-rest encryption | Artifacts, builds and keys stored by the service                         | The `encryption` block of each [blob storage block](/docs/platform/updates/reference/configuration#blob-storage-blocks) |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Signing [#signing]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Signing is optional. When you ask for it, `swugenerator` calls the configured signer script (`sign_script_path`, which is `sign_kms.sh`), and the script asks the Lamassu KMS (`kms_endpoint`) to sign. The private key never reaches the machine that builds the package.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * For `.swu` builds both settings must be set: the service refuses a signing request when either is missing.
  * Signing a manifest, a `non-swu` package or a hawkBit `raw` module calls the KMS directly from the service and needs only `kms_endpoint`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Select the key in the build request with `signature_key_id`, `signature_alg_name` (default `RSASSA_PSS_SHA_256`; `-` and `_` are interchangeable) and `signature_certificate` (PEM). The three fields go together: a request with a key but no algorithm or certificate is refused, never built unsigned.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Set up signing [#set-up-signing]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Create the key and a certificate [#create-the-key-and-a-certificate]

      In the Lamassu KMS, create (or choose) the signing key and issue a certificate for it from a CA your devices trust. See [Keys and cryptographic engines](/docs/platform/pki/key-management). The key ID is your `signature_key_id`.
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Configure the service [#configure-the-service]

      Set `kms_endpoint` and `sign_script_path` (`/app/sign_kms.sh` in the image). `swugenerator` calls the script with the key ID, the KMS URL, the algorithm and the path of the certificate file, which the script requires. The script writes a debug log to `/tmp/sign_kms_debug.log`.
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Send the signature fields in the build [#send-the-signature-fields-in-the-build]

      Include `signature_key_id`, `signature_alg_name` and `signature_certificate` in the build body. In `hawkbit` mode they go in the module build body.
    </Step>
  </Steps>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Callout type="warn" title="The KMS must return a CMS (PKCS7) signature">
    SWUpdate verifies a `.swu` with a CMS `SignedData` signature, and the service requires CMS for the manifests it signs itself. A Lamassu KMS that ignores the `Accept` header and answers with a bare signature in a JSON envelope produces a signature no device can verify. Where the service signs itself (version manifests, set manifests, raw-module checksums) it refuses such an answer and the operation fails with `the KMS did not return a PKCS7/CMS signature`. The SWU signer script does not check the format: it unwraps the answer and embeds it, so against a KMS without CMS support a `.swu` build can succeed and still be rejected by a device that sets `public-key-file`. Test one signed build on a real device before you rely on a KMS version.
  </Callout>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `sign_kms_nocms.sh` is a variant of the script that takes no certificate. The service's own manifest signing is separate: it always sends the certificate and refuses to sign without one.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  TLS towards the KMS: in `native` mode the service's KMS client skips certificate verification, and `sign_kms.sh` calls `curl -k`. In `hawkbit` mode the service's own KMS calls verify the certificate, but the SWU signer script still uses `curl -k`. Reach the KMS over an internal address you trust. See [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Signed manifests [#signed-manifests]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Each built version also has a **manifest**, an anti-rollback record of what the version contains: name, group, version, packaging, artifacts with their SHA-256, the deliverable and, in `hawkbit` mode, the exact modules and versions that compose the set. A manifest is valid for 5 years (`expires_at`). It is signed with the KMS key when the build carried signing fields, and stored unsigned otherwise (the service logs a warning). If a signing key is configured but the manifest cannot be signed, the build fails.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Read it with:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  ```text
  GET /updates/v1/groups/:groupID/distribution-sets/:name/versions/:version/signature
  GET /updates/v1/groups/:groupID/distribution-sets/:name/signature        # current version
  ```
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The response has `manifest` (the exact bytes the signature covers), `signature` (base64 CMS), `algorithm`, `certificate` (PEM), `signed_at` and `expires_at`. In `hawkbit` mode `stale: true` means a signed manifest exists but the set's contents changed since, so the manifest returned describes the set as it is now. The `artifact_signatures` [capability](/docs/platform/updates/reference/capabilities) reports whether the active backend provides it.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Encryption modes [#encryption-modes]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Mode       | What you get                                                                      | `native` | `hawkbit`                                                                      |
  | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | None       | One unencrypted deliverable                                                       | Yes      | Yes                                                                            |
  | Shared     | One deliverable encrypted with one key, served to every device                    | Yes      | Yes, through the module build endpoints, when the build pipeline is configured |
  | Per-device | One deliverable per device, each encrypted with that device's own key from SymKMS | Yes      | No                                                                             |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The build body decides the mode:
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * **Shared**: send `user`, `encryption_key_name` and `encryption_alg_name`. A `.swu` build is refused without the algorithm. A `.../package` build picks AES-GCM from the key length and only records the name you send.
  * **Per-device**: send `encryption_alg_name` **without** `user` or `encryption_key_name`. This holds for `.../package` too: sending the algorithm is what selects per-device mode, and omitting it builds an unencrypted package.
  * **None**: send neither.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Other build fields: `sw_desc_encrypted` also encrypts the sw-description itself, and `selected_artifact_ids` lists the artifacts the build includes. In `native` mode a `.swu` build with no selected artifacts fails.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  In `hawkbit` mode `POST .../swu` returns `501`. Send the same signing and encryption fields to the module build instead: `POST /updates/v1/softwaremodules/by-id/:moduleID/build` (for `swu-build` and `raw` modules). See [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode#create-and-build-a-pack).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The sw-description must mark the artifacts to encrypt with `encrypted = true;`. A per-device build is refused when no artifact is marked, because the key alone does nothing.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Algorithms [#algorithms]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The `algorithm` of a SymKMS key and the `encryption_alg_name` of a build use these names.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Algorithm                                   | Key length |
  | ------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
  | `AES-128-CBC`, `AES-128-CTR`, `AES-128-GCM` | 16 bytes   |
  | `AES-192-CBC`, `AES-192-CTR`, `AES-192-GCM` | 24 bytes   |
  | `AES-256-CBC`, `AES-256-CTR`, `AES-256-GCM` | 32 bytes   |
  | `ASCON-128`, `ASCON-128A`                   | 16 bytes   |
  | `ASCON-80PQ`                                | 20 bytes   |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * **SymKMS key names**: matching ignores case, and `_` and `-` are interchangeable (`aes_256_gcm` is stored as `AES-256-GCM`). The separators of the name must still be there: `ascon128a` is not `ASCON-128A`. A key whose length does not match its algorithm is rejected when it is created.
  * **Build names**: `encryption_alg_name` is passed to `swugenerator` as it is. Case is ignored, but the hyphens are required: `aes-256-gcm` works, `AES_256_GCM` is rejected. If the name differs from the algorithm stored with the key, the service logs a warning and uses the name from the request.
  * **`non-swu` packages** (`.../package`, and `hawkbit` `raw` modules) are always encrypted with **AES-GCM**, chosen by key length (16, 24 or 32 bytes). The requested name is only recorded, and a 20-byte Ascon-80pq key is refused. The result is `nonce || ciphertext`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The service generates the IV or nonce. In `native` mode the algorithm and, for shared-key packs, the IV are passed to the device in the WFX job. A per-device build draws a fresh IV for each device and does not record it in the job, so the job carries the algorithm only. The job fields are listed in [Connect a device](/docs/platform/updates/guides/connect-a-device).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Set up per-device encryption [#set-up-per-device-encryption]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  <Steps>
    <Step>
      Create a key per device [#create-a-key-per-device]

      In SymKMS, `POST /symkms/v1/` with `user_id`, an `algorithm` from the table and a `key` (hex or base64) of the right length.
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Assign it to the device [#assign-it-to-the-device]

      `POST /symkms/v1/inventory/:deviceID/keys/:keyID` with a body `{"purpose":"firmware-encryption"}` and an optional `expires_at` (RFC 3339). A per-device build asks for each device's `firmware-encryption` key.
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Put the same key on the device [#put-the-same-key-on-the-device]

      In the form SWUpdate expects (its `-K` key file, with the key, IV and algorithm).
    </Step>

    <Step>
      Build [#build]

      Send `encryption_alg_name` and no `user` or `encryption_key_name`. The sw-description must mark an artifact `encrypted = true;`.
    </Step>
  </Steps>
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  **Key purposes.** The conventional purposes are `firmware-encryption`, `config-encryption` and `mac-verification`. The purpose is a placeholder: any value is accepted, and a binding with an empty purpose acts as a wildcard that matches any lookup. This is intentional while per-purpose keys are rolled out. An exact (case-insensitive) match wins over a wildcard, and among equals the most recent assignment wins. Expired or revoked bindings are skipped.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  **Coverage.** A device with no `firmware-encryption` key is skipped (the reason reads `no firmware-encryption key assigned` for `.swu` builds). The build still succeeds if at least one device was covered, and the pack records the coverage: read `built_device_count`, `total_device_count` and `uncovered_devices` on it. A launch on a pack with uncovered devices is refused with `400`, and there is no override: assign the missing keys and build again. If no device was covered, the build itself fails.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  **Cost.** A per-device build runs one `swugenerator` process per device, in parallel up to the CPU available to the container. On a 100 MB artifact, one device costs roughly half a second of encryption, plus about three seconds more if the sw-description asks for gzip compression. Size the container accordingly: see [Resource sizing](/docs/platform/updates/operations#resource-sizing). Builds of the same pack are serialized: a second build or version bump while one runs answers `409`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  SymKMS [#symkms]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  SymKMS is the embedded symmetric key service, served by the same process under `/symkms/v1`. It stores keys, assigns them to devices, and can also encrypt, decrypt and compute MACs. Keys are stored in the `symkms` blob store, optionally with at-rest encryption. Create keys with the correct length for their algorithm: random bytes, never a passphrase.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Task                                                     | Route                                                                          |
  | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | Store a key                                              | `POST /symkms/v1/`                                                             |
  | List keys of a user                                      | `GET /symkms/v1/?user_id=...`                                                  |
  | Delete a key                                             | `DELETE /symkms/v1/:keyID?user_id=...`                                         |
  | Assign or revoke a key for a device                      | `POST` or `DELETE /symkms/v1/inventory/:deviceID/keys/:keyID`                  |
  | A device's active key (privileged, returns key material) | `GET /symkms/v1/inventory/:deviceID/key?purpose=...`                           |
  | Which devices use a key                                  | `GET /symkms/v1/inventory/by-key/:keyID`                                       |
  | A device's key bindings                                  | `GET /symkms/v1/inventory/:deviceID`                                           |
  | Encrypt, decrypt                                         | `POST /symkms/v1/encrypt`, `POST /symkms/v1/decrypt`                           |
  | MAC and verify                                           | `POST /symkms/v1/mac`, `POST /symkms/v1/mac/verify` (and the `/file` variants) |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Request bodies [#request-bodies]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Route                        | Body (JSON)                                                                                                                      |
  | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `POST /symkms/v1/`           | `user_id`, `algorithm`, `key` (hex or base64; hex is tried first), optional `id`. `user_id`, `algorithm` and `key` are required. |
  | `POST /symkms/v1/encrypt`    | `user_id`, `key_name`, `algorithm`, `plaintext` (base64), optional `iv`, optional `format`.                                      |
  | `POST /symkms/v1/decrypt`    | `user_id`, `key_name`, `algorithm`, `ciphertext`, `iv`, optional `format`.                                                       |
  | `POST /symkms/v1/mac`        | `user_id`, `key_name`, `mac_algorithm`, `data` (base64). The MAC is returned as hex.                                             |
  | `POST /symkms/v1/mac/verify` | The same as `/mac`, plus `mac` (hex).                                                                                            |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  * `format` is `ciphertext` (hex, the default), `base64`, or `cms` (`pkcs7` is an alias): a PEM-encoded CMS structure that embeds the algorithm and IV. With `cms`, `decrypt` can omit `algorithm` and `iv`.
  * The server generates the nonce for GCM, CTR and Ascon: **a caller-supplied `iv` is refused** for those algorithms. Only CBC accepts one (16 bytes). The response carries the `iv` used (hex).
  * `mac_algorithm` is `HMAC-SHA3-256`, `AES-CMAC` or `ASCON-MAC`. The `/file` variants take the data as `multipart/form-data`.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  `GET /symkms/v1/:keyID/raw?user_id=...` and `GET /symkms/v1/inventory/:deviceID/key` return raw key material and are privileged: the Updates service itself calls them during a build. The service has no authentication of its own, so restrict these routes at a gateway. See [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security).
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  The same SymKMS routes can run as their own process (`cmd/symkms`) instead of inside the monolith. See [Configuration](/docs/platform/updates/reference/configuration#symkms-as-its-own-process).
</div>


# Troubleshooting (/docs/pr-preview/pr-56/platform/updates/troubleshooting)



<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Diagnose one operation at a time. Note the backend (`GET /updates/v1/capabilities` shows it), the endpoint, the HTTP status and the `err` text of the response body: errors are returned as `{"err": "..."}`. If your problem is not here, check [Limitations](/docs/platform/updates/limitations) first.
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  HTTP status codes [#http-status-codes]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Status | Meaning                                                                                                                    |
  | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `400`  | The request or the current state of the resource does not allow the operation. The message says what to change.            |
  | `403`  | A policy refuses the operation.                                                                                            |
  | `404`  | The resource does not exist. Another group's launch also answers `404`.                                                    |
  | `409`  | A conflicting operation is in progress, or the version is already built.                                                   |
  | `413`  | A file is larger than `max_artifact_size_mb`.                                                                              |
  | `500`  | An unexpected failure. Some validation errors still answer `500` (see below).                                              |
  | `501`  | The active backend does not support the operation. Read the [capabilities](/docs/platform/updates/reference/capabilities). |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Starting the service [#starting-the-service]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom or message                                                            | Likely cause                                                                  | Fix                                                                                                                          |
  | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `docker compose up` fails with a network error                                | The `ota-net` network does not exist                                          | `docker network create ota-net`                                                                                              |
  | Docker build cannot find `lamassuiot/core`                                    | The build context is not the parent of the checkout                           | Build with the context that contains `ota/`, `lamassuiot/core` and `lamassuiot/sdk`. `docker compose build updates` uses it. |
  | The service ignores `OTA_CONFIG_FILE` and logs a warning                      | The file could not be loaded, so it fell back to `/etc/lamassuiot/config.yml` | Check the path and the YAML. In the image the fallback is the repository's developer configuration.                          |
  | `workflow_file "..." must contain "direct"`                                   | `workflow_file` does not name the `direct` workflow                           | Point it at `wfx.workflow.dau.direct.yml` or a path containing `direct`.                                                     |
  | `failed to list existing WFX workflows`                                       | `wfx_endpoint` is wrong or WFX is down                                        | Use the **management** port (`8081` inside the Compose network, `9081` on the host) and check that `custom-wfx` runs.        |
  | Postgres reports that database `updates` does not exist                       | The database is not created by the service                                    | Create it (Docker Compose does it through `init.sql`).                                                                       |
  | `mode is "hawkbit" but hawkbit.base_url is not configured`                    | Missing key                                                                   | Set `hawkbit.base_url`.                                                                                                      |
  | `mode is "hawkbit" but storage (Postgres) is not configured`                  | `storage.hostname` is empty                                                   | Set the `storage` block.                                                                                                     |
  | `S3 bucket "x" is not accessible at ...`                                      | Wrong bucket, endpoint or credentials, or the bucket does not exist           | Fix the `s3_*` keys of the block named in the error. The bucket must already exist.                                          |
  | `local encryption key must be exactly 32 bytes`                               | `encryption.local_key` is not 32 bytes of hex                                 | Use 64 hex characters (`openssl rand -hex 32`).                                                                              |
  | `could not configure leader election: the service account may not ... Leases` | The pod cannot use Leases and `leaderElection.mode` is `kubernetes`           | Grant the Role the chart provides (`serviceAccount.create: true`), or set `leaderElection.mode: database`.                   |
  | `not running inside a Kubernetes cluster`                                     | `leader_election.mode: kubernetes` outside a cluster                          | Use empty (auto) or `database`.                                                                                              |
  | `builds.presign: ...` or `hawkbit.artifact_store.presign: ...`                | The presigned-download settings of that block are invalid                     | See [Downloads and presigned URLs](#downloads-and-presigned-urls).                                                           |
  | The hawkBit container exits                                                   | S3 storage is selected for hawkBit and the bucket is unreachable              | Fix the S3 settings, or use `HAWKBIT_ARTIFACT_STORAGE=fs`. hawkBit never falls back to local disk silently.                  |
  | `/health` answers but WFX calls fail                                          | `/health` does not check dependencies                                         | Check `wfx_endpoint` and that WFX is running.                                                                                |
  | Debug output shows secrets                                                    | `app.logs.level: debug` prints the configuration                              | Use `info`. See [Security](/docs/platform/updates/security).                                                                 |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  API calls [#api-calls]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom or message                                                                                             | Likely cause                                                                                 | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `501 Not Implemented`                                                                                          | The active backend does not support the operation                                            | Read `GET /updates/v1/capabilities`. In `hawkbit` mode, `POST .../swu` and `.../package` always answer `501`: build the modules in the catalog.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
  | `409` `update pack version X is already built; create a new version ...`                                       | You changed a built version                                                                  | Native mode: `POST .../new` with `{"version":"x.y.z"}` greater than the current one, then upload the sw-description again (it is not carried over) and give any re-uploaded artifact a higher `version`. `hawkbit` mode: see the next row.                                                                                             |
  | `hawkbit mode: cannot ... here — a software module linked to a distribution set is frozen` (`400`)             | Pack-scoped edits are refused in `hawkbit` mode                                              | Unlink the module, change and build it in the catalog, link it again. Or release a new version of the module and create a pack from it under another name: pack names are unique per group, and an `os` module cannot be swapped on an existing pack. See [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode#create-and-build-a-pack). |
  | `409` `... is being built or changed by another request; retry when it finishes`                               | Two builds, or a build and a change, on the same pack or module                              | Wait and retry. The lock is released when the operation ends or fails.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
  | `409` on create                                                                                                | A pack with that name exists in the group                                                    | Pick another name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
  | `413` `file "x" is N MiB; the maximum upload size is M MiB`                                                    | The file exceeds `max_artifact_size_mb`                                                      | Raise it, and the limits of every proxy in front. See [Operations](/docs/platform/updates/operations#upload-size-and-proxies). A proxy answering `413` with its own body (for example nginx's default 1 MiB) is the proxy, not the service.                                                                                            |
  | Upload `400` mentioning content that contradicts the filename                                                  | A file named `.swu` is not a SWU                                                             | Upload a real `.swu`, or rename the file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
  | Artifact upload fails with `500` and `version X must be greater than the current latest version`               | Artifact names are global, and a name can only be reused with a higher `version`             | Give the new file a higher `version`, or a new artifact name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
  | `Cannot create launch: update pack 'x' has not been built yet` (`400`)                                         | The pack is still a draft                                                                    | Build it first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
  | `Cannot create launch: update pack "x" is per-device encrypted and only N of M devices have a package` (`400`) | Some devices have no key                                                                     | Assign the missing keys and build again. There is no override.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
  | `approval_threshold and error_threshold must be between 0 and 100`                                             | Thresholds are percentages                                                                   | Use `0`-`100`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
  | `launch X is paused; resume it first` (`400`)                                                                  | The launch was paused                                                                        | Call `resume`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
  | `test device X cannot act as this group's canary: device X does not exist` (`hawkbit` mode)                    | The canary check runs before the group's devices exist in hawkBit                            | Run a dry run without `test_device_id` first (`POST .../launch?dry_run=true`), which registers the devices as targets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
  | The device registry or KMS answers `401`                                                                       | The service always sends `X-Principal-ID: admin-mode`, and the gateway in between rejects it | Point `dms_endpoint` and `kms_endpoint` at the internal service addresses, or allow that header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Builds [#builds]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom or message                                                                                      | Likely cause                                                                             | Fix                                                                                                                                  |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `no sw-descriptor uploaded for update pack "x" vN`                                                      | The version has no sw-description (each version needs its own)                           | Upload it.                                                                                                                           |
  | `failed to read binaries directory` or `binaries directory is empty`                                    | `native` mode: nothing was staged, because the build body has no `selected_artifact_ids` | Pass the artifact IDs. See the [publish guide](/docs/platform/updates/guides/publish-and-roll-out).                                  |
  | `swugenerator failed: exit status N`                                                                    | The tool rejected its input. Its own message is in the service log                       | Check the sw-description, the file names it references, the algorithm spelling (`aes-256-gcm`, hyphens required) and the key length. |
  | `signing requested but sign_script_path/kms endpoint are not configured`                                | A `.swu` was asked to be signed without both settings                                    | Set `sign_script_path` and `kms_endpoint`.                                                                                           |
  | `signing requires key id, algorithm and certificate together`                                           | A partial signature request                                                              | Send all three `signature_*` fields.                                                                                                 |
  | `failed to sign version manifest: the KMS did not return a PKCS7/CMS signature`                         | The KMS answered with a bare signature                                                   | Use a KMS version that returns CMS. See [Signing and encryption](/docs/platform/updates/signing-and-encryption#signing).             |
  | `symKMS SDK client is not configured`                                                                   | `symkms_endpoint` is empty                                                               | Set it. In `hawkbit` mode also set the `symkms` block so the routes exist.                                                           |
  | `failed to fetch key "k" via symKMS`                                                                    | Wrong key ID or `user`, or the endpoint points at another instance                       | The key belongs to its `user_id`; `symkms_endpoint` must be this instance's own address and port.                                    |
  | Per-device build fails mentioning `encrypted = true`                                                    | No artifact in the sw-description is marked `encrypted = true;`                          | Mark the artifacts to encrypt.                                                                                                       |
  | `no devices found for DMS X` or `none of the N devices ... have a key assigned for firmware-encryption` | The group has no devices in the registry, or none has a key                              | Check the group in Lamassu IoT and `dms_endpoint`; assign `firmware-encryption` keys.                                                |
  | `hawkbit mode: this deployment has no SWU builder configured` (`501`)                                   | `swugenerator_path` is empty                                                             | Set it, or upload a prebuilt `.swu` module.                                                                                          |
  | `hawkbit mode: this deployment has no SymKMS configured` or `... no KMS endpoint configured` (`501`)    | Encryption or signing asked without `symkms_endpoint` or `kms_endpoint`                  | Set them.                                                                                                                            |
  | `software module "x" ... is N MB and encrypting it needs about M MB in memory`                          | `build_memory_limit_mb` refuses the build                                                | Sign without encrypting, split the file, or raise the limit together with the pod's memory.                                          |
  | `... is already built; ... release a new version of it to build again`                                  | A build replaces the module's input files                                                | Create a new version of the module.                                                                                                  |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Downloads and presigned URLs [#downloads-and-presigned-urls]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom or message                                                | Likely cause                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                               |
  | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `404` `SWU not available for device D on pack "x" vN`             | The pack is per-device encrypted and has no package for that device (its key was missing at build time, or the pack inherited per-device mode from an earlier version), or the build file is gone from the store | Assign the device's key and build a new version. To avoid inheriting, use a separate pack for each encryption variant (see [Limitations](/docs/platform/updates/limitations#packs-and-versions)). |
  | Startup: `presign needs its own credential`                       | `presign` is enabled without a signing credential                                                                                                                                                                | Set `presign.access_key_id[_file]` and `secret_access_key[_file]`, a read-only pair.                                                                                                              |
  | Startup: `the presign credential can WRITE`                       | The signing credential has write access                                                                                                                                                                          | Give it a read-only policy on the objects it serves.                                                                                                                                              |
  | Startup: `presign signs with the storage's own credential`        | Same key as the storage                                                                                                                                                                                          | Create a separate read-only key.                                                                                                                                                                  |
  | Startup: `the store does not accept the presign credential`       | The store does not know the key, or the signature does not match                                                                                                                                                 | Create the user in the store; check region and endpoint.                                                                                                                                          |
  | Startup: `presign cannot be combined with client-side encryption` | `encryption.type` is not `none` on that block                                                                                                                                                                    | Use store-side encryption, or disable `presign`.                                                                                                                                                  |
  | Startup: `presign.public_endpoint must be an http(s) origin`      | The value has no scheme, or has a path                                                                                                                                                                           | Use an origin such as `https://updates.example.com`.                                                                                                                                              |
  | The device gets `403` from the store after the `302`              | The URL expired before the device started the GET, the signed `Host` is not what the device used (`public_endpoint` wrong), the signing key cannot read that prefix, or clocks differ                            | Retry (a fresh URL is issued per request); check `ttl`, `public_endpoint` and the key's policy.                                                                                                   |
  | Downloads stream through the service despite `presign`            | A `HEAD` request, an artifact download by ID in `native` mode, a store without `presign` for that block, or the signing failed (logged)                                                                          | Only builds in `native` mode and the S3 plugin objects in `hawkbit` mode are redirected.                                                                                                          |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Updates not reaching devices [#updates-not-reaching-devices]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                                             | Likely cause                                                                                                      | Fix                                                                                                                                         |
  | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Devices cannot download the `.swu` (`native` mode)                                  | `update_domain` is not reachable from the device, or is not the full `.../updates/v1/` base with a trailing slash | Use an address the device can resolve. The Helm chart default lacks `/updates`.                                                             |
  | `hawkbit` mode: a device gets `401` from DDI                                        | hawkBit refuses devices that do not authenticate                                                                  | Enable and use a hawkBit device authenticator. See [hawkBit mode](/docs/platform/updates/hawkbit-mode#device-authentication-in-production). |
  | `hawkbit` mode: a device gets `429`                                                 | hawkBit's own DoS filter, which limits how often a device may call it                                             | Slow the polling and feedback of the device.                                                                                                |
  | `hawkbit` mode: the launch stays `running` with no progress                         | The devices never contacted hawkBit, or they poll a different hawkBit                                             | Check which hawkBit the devices poll, and that the targets exist. A rollout group cannot advance until its devices poll.                    |
  | `hawkbit` mode: devices are not found in the group                                  | `dms_endpoint` is not set, so groups are the `group:<id>` target tags                                             | Set `dms_endpoint`, or tag the targets.                                                                                                     |
  | A `phased` launch stays at `CREATED` (`native` mode)                                | In the `phased` workflow some steps are made by WFX or an operator                                                | Confirm them through WFX, or use `direct`.                                                                                                  |
  | A `non-swu` launch shows SWU states (`native` mode)                                 | It was created with `workflow_type: direct`                                                                       | Use `download-install`.                                                                                                                     |
  | The device installs and shows the old version                                       | The payload version was not changed                                                                               | Bump the version before building.                                                                                                           |
  | The device ignores new deployments                                                  | SWUpdate keeps the update state of an earlier install as pending test (`ustate=1`) and refuses a new one          | Confirm or reset the device's update state. This is a device setting, not a service one.                                                    |
  | The device rejects the `.swu` and the error mentions decryption or an invalid image | The `.swu` is unsigned while the device requires a signature, or the signature is not CMS                         | Sign it with a KMS that returns CMS. A signature failure can be reported as an encryption error.                                            |
  | The device fails to decrypt                                                         | The key used to build differs from the device's key, or the algorithm spelling differs                            | Use the same key and algorithm. Check the assignment in SymKMS.                                                                             |
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  Scaling and background work [#scaling-and-background-work]
</div>

<div className="lm-diff-ins lm-diff-block">
  | Symptom                                                  | Likely cause                                                                | Fix                                                                                                                                                |
  | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Pods cannot start on different nodes                     | The `ReadWriteOnce` volume (both modes while `persistence.enabled` is true) | Set `persistence.enabled: false` and move `artifacts`, `builds` and `symkms` to S3. See [Operations](/docs/platform/updates/operations#scale-out). |
  | Campaign batches never advance (`native` mode)           | Leader election is failing, or WFX events are not arriving                  | Check the Leases and the RBAC, or set `leaderElection.mode: database`. The log line `leadership acquired` appears on the leader.                   |
  | Scheduled launches never start (`native` mode)           | The same background work, which runs on the leader                          | As above.                                                                                                                                          |
